verses.1:1: The first account I prepared, O Theophilus, concerning all things that Jesus began both to do and to teach,
verses.1:2: until the day in which, having given commandments through the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom He had chosen, He was taken up;
verses.1:3: to whom He also presented Himself alive after His suffering by many unmistakable proofs, appearing to them throughout forty days and speaking of the things concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.1:4: And while gathered together with them, He charged them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to await the promise of the Father, "which you have heard from Me;
verses.1:5: for John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized in the Holy Spirit not many days from now."
verses.1:6: So when they had come together, they were asking Him, saying, "Lord, is it at this time that You are restoring the kingdom to Israel?"
verses.1:7: And He said to them, "It is not yours to know times or seasons which the Father has set within His own authority,
verses.1:8: but you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit comes upon you, and you shall be My witnesses both in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the uttermost part of the earth."
verses.1:9: And having spoken these things, while they were watching, He was lifted up, and a cloud received Him from before their eyes.
verses.1:10: And as they were gazing intently into heaven while He was going, behold, two men stood beside them in white garments,
verses.1:11: who also said, "Men of Galilee, why do you stand looking into heaven? This very Jesus, who was taken up from you into heaven, shall come in the same manner in which you beheld Him going into heaven."
verses.1:12: Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which lies near Jerusalem, a Sabbath day's journey away.
verses.1:13: And when they had entered, they went up into the upper room where they were staying: Peter and John and James and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James the son of Alphaeus and Simon the Zealot and Judas the son of James.
verses.1:14: All these were continuing steadfastly with one accord in prayer, together with the women and Mary the mother of Jesus, and with His brothers.
verses.1:15: And in those days Peter stood up in the midst of the brethren and said (now the company of persons gathered together was about one hundred and twenty):
verses.1:16: "Men and brethren, it was necessary that the Scripture be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit spoke beforehand through the mouth of David concerning Judas, who became a guide to those who seized Jesus,
verses.1:17: for he was numbered among us and obtained the allotted share of this ministry."
verses.1:18: (Now this man acquired a field from the reward of iniquity, and falling headlong, he burst open in the middle, and all his inward parts poured out.
verses.1:19: And it became known to all those dwelling in Jerusalem, so that in their own language that field was called Akeldama, that is, Field of Blood.)
verses.1:20: "For it is written in the Book of Psalms, 'Let his habitation become desolate, and let no one dwell in it,' and, 'Let another take his office.'
verses.1:21: Therefore, from among the men who accompanied us during all the time that the Lord Jesus went in and out among us,
verses.1:22: beginning from the baptism of John until the day in which He was taken up from us, one of these must become with us a witness of His resurrection."
verses.1:23: And they set forward two: Joseph called Barsabbas, who was also named Justus, and Matthias.
verses.1:24: And praying, they said, "You, O Lord, who know the hearts of all, make known which one of these two You have chosen
verses.1:25: to receive the place of this ministry and apostleship, from which Judas turned aside to go to his own place."
verses.1:26: And they cast lots for them, and the lot fell upon Matthias, and he was numbered together with the eleven apostles.
verses.2:1: And when the day of Pentecost had come in full, they were all together in one place.
verses.2:2: And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a violent, rushing wind, and it filled the whole house where they were sitting.
verses.2:3: And there appeared to them tongues as of fire, distributed among them, and one rested upon each of them.
verses.2:4: And they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and began to speak in other tongues, just as the Spirit granted them utterance.
verses.2:5: Now there were Jews residing in Jerusalem, devout men from every nation under heaven.
verses.2:6: And when this sound occurred, the multitude came together and was confounded, because each one heard them speaking in his own language.
verses.2:7: And they were amazed and marveled, saying, "Behold, are not all these who are speaking Galileans?
verses.2:8: And how do we hear, each one in our own language in which we were born?
verses.2:9: Parthians and Medes and Elamites, and those dwelling in Mesopotamia, Judea and Cappadocia, Pontus and Asia,
verses.2:10: Phrygia and Pamphylia, Egypt and the districts of Libya near Cyrene, and sojourners from Rome,
verses.2:11: both Jews and proselytes, Cretans and Arabs—we hear them declaring in our own tongues the mighty works of God."
verses.2:12: And they were all astounded and perplexed, saying one to another, "What does this mean?"
verses.2:13: But others, scoffing, said, "They are filled with sweet wine."
verses.2:14: But Peter, taking his stand with the eleven, lifted up his voice and declared to them, "Men of Judea and all who dwell in Jerusalem, let this be known to you, and give ear to my words.
verses.2:15: For these men are not drunk, as you suppose, for it is the third hour of the day;
verses.2:16: rather, this is what was spoken through the prophet Joel:
verses.2:17: 'And it shall be in the last days, says God, I will pour out from My Spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy, and your young men shall behold visions, and your aged men shall dream dreams.
verses.2:18: And indeed upon My menservants and upon My maidservants in those days I will pour out from My Spirit, and they shall prophesy.
verses.2:19: And I will set forth wonders in heaven above and signs upon the earth beneath: blood and fire and vapor of smoke.
verses.2:20: The sun shall be turned to darkness, and the moon to blood, before the day of the Lord comes, great and glorious.
verses.2:21: And it shall be that everyone who calls upon the name of the Lord shall be saved.'
verses.2:22: Men of Israel, hear these words: Jesus the Nazarene, a man attested to you by God with deeds of power and wonders and signs which God performed through Him in your midst, just as you yourselves know—
verses.2:23: this Man, delivered up by the appointed counsel and foreknowledge of God, you nailed to a cross and slew by the hand of lawless men;
verses.2:24: whom God raised up, having loosed the pangs of death, because it was not possible for Him to be held fast by it.
verses.2:25: For David says concerning Him, 'I beheld the Lord before Me continually, because He is at My right hand, that I should not be shaken.
verses.2:26: Therefore My heart was glad, and My tongue exulted; moreover, My flesh also shall dwell in hope;
verses.2:27: because You will not abandon My soul to Hades, nor will You allow Your Holy One to see corruption.
verses.2:28: You have made known to Me the paths of life; You will fill Me with gladness in Your presence.'
verses.2:29: Men and brethren, let me speak plainly to you concerning the patriarch David, that he both died and was buried, and his tomb is among us to this very day.
verses.2:30: Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne,
verses.2:31: foreseeing this, he spoke concerning the resurrection of the Christ, that He was neither abandoned to Hades, nor did His flesh see corruption.
verses.2:32: This Jesus God raised up, of which we are all witnesses.
verses.2:33: Being therefore exalted to the right hand of God, and having received from the Father the promise of the Holy Spirit, He has poured out this which you see and hear.
verses.2:34: For David did not ascend into the heavens, yet he himself says, 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit at My right hand,
verses.2:35: until I make Your enemies a footstool for Your feet."'
verses.2:36: Therefore let all the house of Israel know with certainty that God has made Him both Lord and Christ—this Jesus whom you crucified."
verses.2:37: Now when they heard this, they were pierced to the heart, and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, "What shall we do, men and brethren?"
verses.2:38: And Peter said to them, "Repent, and let each one of you be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ for the forgiveness of your sins, and you shall receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
verses.2:39: For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all who are far off, as many as the Lord our God shall call to Himself."
verses.2:40: And with many other words he solemnly testified and exhorted them, saying, "Be saved from this crooked generation."
verses.2:41: So those who received his word were baptized, and on that day there were added about three thousand souls.
verses.2:42: And they continued steadfastly in the teaching of the apostles and the fellowship, in the breaking of bread and the prayers.
verses.2:43: And awe came upon every soul, and many wonders and signs were being done through the apostles.
verses.2:44: And all who believed were together and held all things in common,
verses.2:45: and they were selling their possessions and goods and distributing them to all, according as anyone had need.
verses.2:46: And continuing steadfastly day by day with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread from house to house, they partook of food with gladness and simplicity of heart,
verses.2:47: praising God and having favor with all the people. And the Lord added to their number day by day those who were being saved.
verses.3:1: Now Peter and John were ascending to the temple at the hour of prayer, the ninth hour.
verses.3:2: And a certain man who had been lame from his mother's womb was being carried, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple called Beautiful, to ask alms from those entering into the temple.
verses.3:3: Seeing Peter and John as they were about to enter the temple, he asked to receive alms.
verses.3:4: Then Peter, gazing intently upon him along with John, said, "Look at us."
verses.3:5: So he gave heed to them, expecting to receive something from them.
verses.3:6: Then Peter said, "Silver and gold I do not possess, yet what I have, this I give to you: In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, walk!"
verses.3:7: And seizing him by the right hand, he raised him up; and at once his feet and ankles were made firm.
verses.3:8: And leaping up, he stood and walked about, and he entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
verses.3:9: And all the people beheld him walking about and praising God.
verses.3:10: And they recognized him, that this was the one who sat for alms at the Beautiful Gate of the temple; and they were filled with wonder and astonishment at what had befallen him.
verses.3:11: Now as he clung to Peter and John, all the people ran together to them in the portico called Solomon's, utterly astonished.
verses.3:12: When Peter saw this, he answered the people: "Men of Israel, why do you marvel at this, or why do you gaze intently at us, as though by our own power or godliness we had caused him to walk?
verses.3:13: The God of Abraham and Isaac and Jacob, the God of our fathers, has glorified His Servant Jesus, whom you indeed handed over and denied before the face of Pilate, when he had decided to release Him.
verses.3:14: Yet you denied the Holy and Righteous One, and asked that a murderer be granted to you,
verses.3:15: and you slew the Author of life, whom God raised from the dead—of which we are witnesses.
verses.3:16: And upon the basis of faith in His name, His name has made firm this man whom you behold and know; and the faith that is through Him has given him this complete soundness in the presence of you all.
verses.3:17: And now, brethren, I know that you acted in ignorance, just as your rulers also did.
verses.3:18: But what God foretold through the mouth of all the prophets, that His Christ should suffer, He has thus fulfilled.
verses.3:19: Repent therefore and turn again, so that your sins may be blotted out,
verses.3:20: that seasons of refreshing may come from the presence of the Lord, and that He may send the Christ appointed beforehand for you, Jesus,
verses.3:21: whom heaven indeed must receive until the times of the restoration of all things, about which God spoke through the mouth of His holy prophets from of old.
verses.3:22: Moses indeed said, 'The Lord our God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from among your brethren; to Him you shall listen in all things, whatever He may speak to you.
verses.3:23: And it shall come to pass that every soul that does not listen to that Prophet shall be utterly destroyed from among the people.'
verses.3:24: Yes, and all the prophets from Samuel and those who came after him, as many as spoke, have also proclaimed these days.
verses.3:25: You are the sons of the prophets and of the covenant that God established with your fathers, saying to Abraham, 'And in your seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed.'
verses.3:26: To you first, God, having raised up His Servant, sent Him to bless you by turning each one away from your iniquities."
verses.4:1: Now while they were speaking to the people, the priests, the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees came upon them,
verses.4:2: being greatly provoked because they were teaching the people and proclaiming in Jesus the resurrection from the dead.
verses.4:3: And they laid hands upon them and placed them in custody until the next day, for evening had already come.
verses.4:4: Yet many of those who heard the word believed, and the number of the men came to be about five thousand.
verses.4:5: And it came to pass on the next day that their rulers, elders, and scribes were assembled in Jerusalem,
verses.4:6: along with Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and as many as belonged to the high-priestly family.
verses.4:7: And having set them in the midst, they inquired, "By what power or in what name did you do this?"
verses.4:8: Then Peter, filled with the Holy Spirit, spoke to them: "Rulers of the people and elders,
verses.4:9: if we are being examined this day concerning a good deed done to an infirm man, by what means this man has been made whole,
verses.4:10: let it be known to you all and to all the people of Israel that by the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom you crucified, whom God raised from the dead—by Him this man stands before you in sound health.
verses.4:11: He is the stone that was despised by you, the builders, which has become the head of the corner.
verses.4:12: And in no other is there salvation; for neither is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we must be saved."
verses.4:13: Now as they beheld the boldness of Peter and John and perceived that they were unlettered and untrained men, they marveled; and they recognized them, that they had been with Jesus.
verses.4:14: And seeing the man who had been healed standing there with them, they had nothing to say in opposition.
verses.4:15: So having ordered them to depart outside the council, they conferred among themselves,
verses.4:16: saying, "What shall we do with these men? For indeed, that a notable sign has taken place through them is manifest to all who dwell in Jerusalem, and we are unable to deny it.
verses.4:17: Yet lest it spread any further among the people, let us threaten them to speak no longer in this name to any man."
verses.4:18: And calling them in, they charged them neither to speak at all nor to teach in the name of Jesus.
verses.4:19: But Peter and John answered and said to them, "Whether it is right before God to heed you rather than God, you yourselves judge;
verses.4:20: for we cannot refrain from speaking of the things that we have seen and heard."
verses.4:21: And after threatening them further, they released them, finding no way to punish them on account of the people, because all were glorifying God for what had come to pass.
verses.4:22: For the man upon whom this sign of healing had been performed was more than forty years old.
verses.4:23: Upon being released, they went to their own companions and reported all that the chief priests and elders had spoken to them.
verses.4:24: And when they heard it, they lifted up their voice to God with one accord and said, "Sovereign Lord, You who made heaven and earth and the sea and all things that are in them,
verses.4:25: who by the Holy Spirit through the mouth of our father David, Your servant, spoke: 'Why did the nations rage, and the peoples devise vain things?
verses.4:26: The kings of the earth took their stand, and the rulers assembled together against the Lord and against His Anointed.'
verses.4:27: For truly in this city both Herod and Pontius Pilate, together with the Gentiles and the peoples of Israel, were assembled against Your holy Servant Jesus, whom You anointed,
verses.4:28: to do whatever Your hand and Your counsel had determined beforehand to come to pass.
verses.4:29: And now, Lord, look upon their threats, and grant to Your bondservants to speak Your word with all boldness,
verses.4:30: as You stretch out Your hand for healing, and as signs and wonders come to pass through the name of Your holy Servant Jesus."
verses.4:31: And when they had prayed, the place where they were assembled was shaken; and they were all filled with the Holy Spirit, and continued to speak the word of God with boldness.
verses.4:32: Now the multitude of those who had believed were of one heart and soul, and not even one said that any of his possessions was his own, but all things were common among them.
verses.4:33: And with great power the apostles rendered their testimony to the resurrection of the Lord Jesus, and great grace was upon them all.
verses.4:34: For neither was there any needy person among them; for as many as owned lands or houses sold them and brought the proceeds of the things that were sold,
verses.4:35: and laid them at the apostles' feet; and it was distributed to each one according as any had need.
verses.4:36: Now Joseph, who was surnamed Barnabas by the apostles—which is translated, Son of Encouragement—a Levite, a Cypriot by birth,
verses.4:37: having a field of his own, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:1: Now a certain man named Ananias, together with his wife Sapphira, sold a possession,
verses.5:2: and he kept back a portion of the proceeds, his wife also being aware of it, and bringing a certain part, he laid it at the feet of the apostles.
verses.5:3: Then Peter said, "Ananias, why has Satan filled your heart, that you should lie to the Holy Spirit and keep back part of the price of the land?
verses.5:4: While it remained, did it not remain your own? And once it was sold, was it not within your own authority? Why have you purposed this deed in your heart? You have not lied to men, but to God."
verses.5:5: And as Ananias heard these words, he fell down and breathed his last; and great fear fell upon all who heard.
verses.5:6: Then the younger men arose, wrapped him up, and carried him out and buried him.
verses.5:7: Now an interval of about three hours passed, and his wife came in, not knowing what had taken place.
verses.5:8: And Peter answered her, "Tell me, did you sell the land for such a price?" And she answered, "Yes, for such a price."
verses.5:9: Then Peter said to her, "Why is it that you have agreed together to test the Spirit of the Lord? Behold, the feet of those who have buried your husband are at the door, and they shall carry you out."
verses.5:10: And instantly she fell down at his feet and breathed her last; and when the young men came in, they found her dead, and carrying her out, they buried her beside her husband.
verses.5:11: And great fear came upon the whole church and upon all who heard these things.
verses.5:12: Now through the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people; and they were all together with one accord in Solomon's Portico.
verses.5:13: Yet none of the rest dared to join them, but the people magnified them,
verses.5:14: and all the more were believers added to the Lord, multitudes of both men and women,
verses.5:15: so that they even carried the sick out into the streets and laid them on cots and mats, that as Peter passed by, at least his shadow might overshadow some of them.
verses.5:16: Also a multitude gathered from the cities around Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those afflicted by unclean spirits, and every one of them was healed.
verses.5:17: Then the high priest rose up, along with all those who were with him—that is, the sect of the Sadducees—and they were filled with jealousy,
verses.5:18: and they laid hands upon the apostles and placed them in the public prison.
verses.5:19: But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison, and leading them out, he said,
verses.5:20: "Go, take your stand in the temple, and speak to the people all the words of this life."
verses.5:21: And when they heard this, they entered the temple at daybreak and began to teach. Now the high priest and those who were with him arrived and convened the Council and all the senate of the sons of Israel, and sent to the prison to have them brought.
verses.5:22: But when the officers arrived, they did not find them in the prison; so they returned and reported,
verses.5:23: saying, "We found the prison locked with all security, and the guards standing at the doors; yet when we opened them, we found no one inside."
verses.5:24: Now when the captain of the temple and the chief priests heard these words, they were greatly perplexed about them, wondering what this would come to.
verses.5:25: Then someone came and reported to them, "Behold, the men whom you put in the prison are standing in the temple and teaching the people."
verses.5:26: Then the captain went with the officers and brought them without force, for they feared the people, lest they should be stoned.
verses.5:27: And having brought them, they set them before the Council. And the high priest questioned them,
verses.5:28: saying, "We strictly charged you not to teach in this name, and behold, you have filled Jerusalem with your teaching, and you intend to bring the blood of this man upon us."
verses.5:29: But Peter and the apostles answered and said, "It is necessary to obey God rather than men.
verses.5:30: The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom you put to death by hanging Him upon a tree.
verses.5:31: This One God has exalted to His right hand as Prince and Savior, to grant repentance to Israel and the forgiveness of sins.
verses.5:32: And we are witnesses of these things, and so is the Holy Spirit, whom God has given to those who obey Him."
verses.5:33: Now when they heard this, they were cut to the quick and desired to slay them.
verses.5:34: But a certain Pharisee in the Council named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law held in honor by all the people, stood up and commanded that the men be put outside for a little while.
verses.5:35: And he said to them, "Men of Israel, take heed to yourselves concerning what you are about to do with these men.
verses.5:36: For before these days Theudas rose up, claiming himself to be somebody, and a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves to him. He was slain, and all who obeyed him were dispersed and came to nothing.
verses.5:37: After him Judas the Galilean rose up in the days of the census and drew away people after himself; he also perished, and all who obeyed him were scattered.
verses.5:38: And now I say to you, keep away from these men and leave them alone; for if this counsel or this work is of men, it shall be overthrown,
verses.5:39: but if it is of God, you will not be able to overthrow them—lest you even be found fighting against God." And they were persuaded by him,
verses.5:40: and when they had called in the apostles and beaten them, they commanded them not to speak in the name of Jesus, and let them go.
verses.5:41: So they departed from the presence of the Council, rejoicing that they had been counted worthy to suffer dishonor on behalf of the Name.
verses.5:42: And every day, in the temple and from house to house, they did not cease teaching and proclaiming the good news that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.6:1: Now in those days, as the disciples were multiplying, there arose a murmuring of the Hellenists against the Hebrews, because their widows were being overlooked in the daily distribution.
verses.6:2: Then the twelve summoned the multitude of the disciples and said, "It is not fitting for us to forsake the word of God in order to serve tables.
verses.6:3: Therefore, brethren, seek out from among you seven men of good report, full of the Spirit and of wisdom, whom we shall appoint over this duty;
verses.6:4: but we shall devote ourselves continually to prayer and to the ministry of the word."
verses.6:5: And the saying pleased the whole multitude; and they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and of the Holy Spirit, and Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas, a proselyte from Antioch,
verses.6:6: whom they set before the apostles; and having prayed, they laid their hands upon them.
verses.6:7: And the word of God continued to increase, and the number of the disciples in Jerusalem multiplied exceedingly, and a great company of the priests became obedient to the faith.
verses.6:8: Now Stephen, full of grace and power, was performing great wonders and signs among the people.
verses.6:9: Then there arose certain ones from the synagogue called that of the Freedmen, as well as Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and some from Cilicia and Asia, disputing with Stephen.
verses.6:10: Yet they were not able to withstand the wisdom and the Spirit by which he spoke.
verses.6:11: Then they secretly instigated men to say, "We have heard him speaking blasphemous words against Moses and God."
verses.6:12: And they stirred up the people, the elders, and the scribes; and coming upon him, they seized him and brought him to the Council.
verses.6:13: They also set up false witnesses who said, "This man does not cease speaking words against the holy place and the law;
verses.6:14: for we have heard him say that this Jesus of Nazareth will destroy this place and change the customs which Moses delivered to us."
verses.6:15: And fixing their eyes upon him, all who sat in the Council saw his countenance as the countenance of an angel.
verses.7:1: Now the high priest said, "Are these things so?"
verses.7:2: And he said, "Men, brethren, and fathers, listen: The God of glory appeared to our father Abraham while he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Haran,
verses.7:3: and said to him, 'Go out from your land and from your kindred, and come into the land that I shall show you.'
verses.7:4: Then he departed from the land of the Chaldeans and dwelt in Haran. And from there, after the death of his father, He removed him into this land in which you now dwell,
verses.7:5: and He did not give him an inheritance in it, not even the breadth of a foot; yet He promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his offspring after him, though he had no child.
verses.7:6: And God spoke thus: that his offspring would be sojourners in a foreign land, and that they would bring them into bondage and afflict them four hundred years;
verses.7:7: 'and the nation to which they shall be in bondage I will judge,' God said, 'and after these things they shall come forth and worship Me in this place.'
verses.7:8: And He gave him the covenant of circumcision; and so he fathered Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaac fathered Jacob, and Jacob the twelve patriarchs.
verses.7:9: And the patriarchs, envious of Joseph, sold him into Egypt; yet God was with him,
verses.7:10: and delivered him from all his afflictions, and granted him favor and wisdom before Pharaoh, king of Egypt; and he appointed him ruler over Egypt and all his household.
verses.7:11: Now a famine came upon all Egypt and Canaan, and great affliction, and our fathers found no sustenance;
verses.7:12: but when Jacob heard that there was grain in Egypt, he sent out our fathers the first time;
verses.7:13: and the second time Joseph was made known to his brothers, and the kindred of Joseph became known to Pharaoh.
verses.7:14: Then Joseph sent and summoned his father Jacob and all his kindred, seventy-five souls in all;
verses.7:15: and Jacob went down into Egypt. And he died, he and our fathers;
verses.7:16: and they were carried over to Shechem and laid in the tomb that Abraham had bought for a sum of silver from the sons of Hamor in Shechem.
verses.7:17: But as the time of the promise drew near, which God had pledged to Abraham, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt,
verses.7:18: until another king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
verses.7:19: He dealt craftily with our race and afflicted our fathers, making them cast out their infants so that they would not be kept alive.
verses.7:20: At that time Moses was born, and he was fair in the sight of God; and he was nurtured three months in the house of his father.
verses.7:21: And when he was cast out, the daughter of Pharaoh took him up and reared him for herself as a son.
verses.7:22: And Moses was trained in all the wisdom of the Egyptians, and he was mighty in his words and works.
verses.7:23: Now when forty years of his life were fulfilled, it entered his heart to visit his brethren, the sons of Israel.
verses.7:24: And seeing one of them being wronged, he defended him and avenged the one who was oppressed by striking down the Egyptian.
verses.7:25: For he supposed that his brethren understood that God was giving them deliverance by his hand, but they did not understand.
verses.7:26: And on the following day he appeared to them as they were fighting, and tried to reconcile them in peace, saying, 'Men, you are brethren; why do you wrong one another?'
verses.7:27: But the one who was wronging his neighbor thrust him aside, saying, 'Who appointed you a ruler and a judge over us?
verses.7:28: Do you intend to slay me in the same manner as you slew the Egyptian yesterday?'
verses.7:29: And at this saying Moses fled and became a sojourner in the land of Midian, where he fathered two sons.
verses.7:30: And when forty years had been fulfilled, an angel appeared to him in the wilderness of Mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush.
verses.7:31: When Moses saw it, he marveled at the sight; and as he drew near to look closely, the voice of the Lord came:
verses.7:32: 'I am the God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' And Moses trembled and did not dare to look.
verses.7:33: Then the Lord said to him, 'Take the sandals off your feet, for the place on which you stand is holy ground.
verses.7:34: I have surely seen the affliction of My people who are in Egypt, and I have heard their groaning, and I have come down to deliver them; and now come, I will send you to Egypt.'
verses.7:35: This Moses whom they rejected, saying, 'Who appointed you a ruler and a judge?'—this man God has sent as both ruler and redeemer by the hand of the angel who appeared to him in the bush.
verses.7:36: This man led them out, performing wonders and signs in the land of Egypt, and in the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for forty years.
verses.7:37: This is the Moses who said to the sons of Israel, 'God will raise up for you a Prophet like me from among your brethren.'
verses.7:38: This is the one who was in the congregation in the wilderness with the angel who spoke to him on Mount Sinai and with our fathers, who received living oracles to give to you;
verses.7:39: whom our fathers refused to obey, but thrust him aside and in their hearts turned back to Egypt,
verses.7:40: saying to Aaron, 'Make for us gods who shall go before us; for as for this Moses who led us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what has happened to him.'
verses.7:41: And they made a calf in those days, and offered a sacrifice to the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their hands.
verses.7:42: Then God turned away and gave them over to worship the host of heaven, as it is written in the book of the Prophets: 'Did you bring Me slain beasts and sacrifices for forty years in the wilderness, O house of Israel?
verses.7:43: Indeed, you took up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of the god Rompha, the images that you made to worship; and I will carry you away beyond Babylon.'
verses.7:44: Our fathers had the tabernacle of testimony in the wilderness, just as He who spoke to Moses directed him to make it according to the pattern that he had seen,
verses.7:45: which our fathers, having received it in turn, also brought in with Joshua when taking possession of the nations whom God drove out before the face of our fathers, until the days of David;
verses.7:46: who found favor in the sight of God and asked to find a dwelling place for the house of Jacob.
verses.7:47: Yet Solomon built a house for Him.
verses.7:48: However, the Most High does not dwell in things made by hands, as the prophet says:
verses.7:49: 'Heaven is My throne, and the earth is the footstool of My feet. What kind of house will you build for Me, says the Lord, or what is the place of My rest?
verses.7:50: Did My hand not make all these things?'
verses.7:51: You stiff-necked people, uncircumcised in hearts and ears, you always resist the Holy Spirit; just as your fathers did, so do you.
verses.7:52: Which of the prophets did your fathers not persecute? And they slew those who foretold the coming of the Righteous One, of whom you have now become the betrayers and murderers,
verses.7:53: you who received the law by the direction of angels, and did not keep it."
verses.7:54: Now when they heard these things, they were cut to their hearts and gnashed their teeth at him.
verses.7:55: But he, full of the Holy Spirit, looked intently into heaven and saw the glory of God, and Jesus standing at the right hand of God,
verses.7:56: and said, "Behold, I see the heavens opened wide, and the Son of Man standing at the right hand of God."
verses.7:57: Then they cried out with a loud voice, covered their ears, and rushed upon him with one accord,
verses.7:58: and casting him out of the city, they began stoning him. And the witnesses laid down their garments at the feet of a young man named Saul.
verses.7:59: And they kept stoning Stephen as he called out and said, "Lord Jesus, receive my spirit."
verses.7:60: Then kneeling down, he cried out with a loud voice, "Lord, do not count this sin against them." And having said this, he fell asleep.
verses.8:1: Now Saul was approving of his execution. And on that day a great persecution broke out against the church in Jerusalem, and all were scattered throughout the regions of Judea and Samaria, except the apostles.
verses.8:2: And devout men bore Stephen away for burial and made a great lamentation over him.
verses.8:3: But Saul was laying waste to the church; going from house to house and dragging away men and women, he delivered them over to prison.
verses.8:4: Therefore those who had been scattered went about proclaiming the good news of the word.
verses.8:5: Then Philip, going down to the city of Samaria, proclaimed the Christ to them.
verses.8:6: And the multitudes with one accord gave heed to the things spoken by Philip, as they heard and beheld the signs that he was performing;
verses.8:7: for from many of those who had unclean spirits, the spirits came forth crying with a loud voice, and many who were paralyzed and lame were healed.
verses.8:8: And there arose great joy in that city.
verses.8:9: Now a certain man by the name of Simon had previously been practicing magic in the city and amazing the nation of Samaria, declaring himself to be someone great,
verses.8:10: to whom all gave heed, from the least to the greatest, saying, "This man is the Power of God that is called Great."
verses.8:11: And they paid attention to him because for a considerable time he had amazed them with his magic arts.
verses.8:12: Yet when they believed Philip as he proclaimed the good news concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, both men and women were baptized.
verses.8:13: And Simon himself also believed; and after being baptized, he stayed continually with Philip, and beholding the signs and great works of power taking place, he was amazed.
verses.8:14: Now when the apostles in Jerusalem heard that Samaria had accepted the word of God, they sent Peter and John to them,
verses.8:15: who went down and prayed concerning them that they might receive the Holy Spirit;
verses.8:16: for He had not yet fallen upon any one of them, but they had only been baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.8:17: Then they laid their hands upon them, and they received the Holy Spirit.
verses.8:18: Now when Simon saw that the Spirit was given through the laying on of the hands of the apostles, he offered them money,
verses.8:19: saying, "Give to me also this authority, so that anyone upon whom I lay my hands may receive the Holy Spirit."
verses.8:20: But Peter said to him, "May your silver perish along with you, because you supposed that you could obtain the gift of God with money.
verses.8:21: You have no part nor lot in this matter, for your heart is not upright in the presence of God.
verses.8:22: Repent therefore of this wickedness of yours, and plead with the Lord that perhaps the intent of your heart may be forgiven you;
verses.8:23: for I perceive that you are in the gall of bitterness and in the fetter of iniquity."
verses.8:24: And Simon answered and said, "Plead with the Lord on my behalf, that none of the things you have spoken may come upon me."
verses.8:25: So after they had solemnly testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they returned toward Jerusalem, proclaiming the good news to many villages of the Samaritans.
verses.8:26: Now an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, "Arise and journey toward the south to the road that descends from Jerusalem to Gaza." This is a desert road.
verses.8:27: And he arose and went; and behold, an Ethiopian man, a eunuch, a high official of Candace, queen of the Ethiopians, who was over all her treasury, had come to Jerusalem to worship,
verses.8:28: and he was returning; and sitting in his chariot, he was reading the prophet Isaiah.
verses.8:29: Then the Spirit said to Philip, "Draw near and join yourself to this chariot."
verses.8:30: So Philip ran up and heard him reading Isaiah the prophet, and said, "Do you truly understand what you are reading?"
verses.8:31: And he said, "How indeed could I, unless someone guides me?" And he urged Philip to come up and sit with him.
verses.8:32: Now the passage of the Scripture that he was reading was this: "Like a sheep He was led to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so He does not open His mouth.
verses.8:33: In humiliation His justice was taken away. Who shall declare His generation? For His life is taken away from the earth."
verses.8:34: And the eunuch answered Philip and said, "I ask you, concerning whom does the prophet say this—concerning himself, or concerning some other man?"
verses.8:35: Then Philip opened his mouth, and beginning from this Scripture, he proclaimed to him the good news of Jesus.
verses.8:36: Now as they journeyed along the road, they came to some water; and the eunuch said, "Behold, water! What prevents me from being baptized?"
verses.8:38: And he commanded the chariot to halt; and both of them went down into the water, Philip and the eunuch, and he baptized him.
verses.8:39: Now when they came up out of the water, the Spirit of the Lord caught Philip away, and the eunuch did not see him anymore, for he went on his way rejoicing.
verses.8:40: But Philip was found at Azotus; and passing through, he proclaimed the good news to all the cities until he came to Caesarea.
verses.9:1: Now Saul, still breathing threats and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord, approached the high priest
verses.9:2: and requested letters from him to the synagogues in Damascus, that if he should find any who belonged to the Way, both men and women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
verses.9:3: And as he journeyed, it came to pass that he drew near to Damascus, and suddenly a light from heaven flashed around him.
verses.9:4: And falling to the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?"
verses.9:5: And he said, "Who are You, Lord?" And He said, "I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.9:6: But arise and enter the city, and it will be told you what you must do."
verses.9:7: Now the men who were traveling with him stood speechless, hearing indeed the voice, yet seeing no one.
verses.9:8: And Saul arose from the ground, yet though his eyes were opened, he saw nothing; so leading him by the hand, they brought him into Damascus.
verses.9:9: And for three days he remained without sight, and neither ate nor drank.
verses.9:10: Now there was a certain disciple in Damascus named Ananias, and the Lord spoke to him in a vision, "Ananias." And he said, "Behold, here I am, Lord."
verses.9:11: And the Lord said to him, "Arise and go to the street called Straight, and inquire at the house of Judas for one named Saul of Tarsus; for behold, he is praying,
verses.9:12: and in a vision he has seen a man named Ananias coming in and laying hands on him, so that he might regain his sight."
verses.9:13: Then Ananias answered, "Lord, I have heard from many concerning this man, how much evil he has done to Your saints in Jerusalem;
verses.9:14: and here he holds authority from the chief priests to bind all who call upon Your name."
verses.9:15: But the Lord said to him, "Go, for this man is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My name before Gentiles and kings and the sons of Israel;
verses.9:16: for I will show him how many things he must suffer for the sake of My name."
verses.9:17: So Ananias departed and entered the house, and laying his hands upon him, he said, "Brother Saul, the Lord has sent me—Jesus, who appeared to you on the road along which you came—that you may regain your sight and be filled with the Holy Spirit."
verses.9:18: And immediately something like scales fell from his eyes, and he regained his sight; and arising, he was baptized,
verses.9:19: and taking food, he was strengthened. Now he spent several days with the disciples in Damascus,
verses.9:20: and immediately in the synagogues he proclaimed Jesus, that He is the Son of God.
verses.9:21: And all who heard him were astonished and said, "Is this not the one who ravaged in Jerusalem those who call upon this name, and had come here for this very purpose, that he might bring them bound before the chief priests?"
verses.9:22: But Saul increased all the more in strength, and confounded the Jews who dwelt in Damascus, proving that this One is the Christ.
verses.9:23: Now when many days had passed, the Jews took counsel together to slay him;
verses.9:24: but their plot became known to Saul. And they kept watch over the gates both day and night, that they might slay him.
verses.9:25: Then his disciples took him by night and let him down through the wall, lowering him in a basket.
verses.9:26: And when he had come to Jerusalem, he sought to join himself to the disciples; yet they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
verses.9:27: But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and recounted to them how on the road he had seen the Lord, and that He had spoken to him, and how in Damascus he had spoken boldly in the name of Jesus.
verses.9:28: So he remained with them, going in and going out in Jerusalem, speaking boldly in the name of the Lord,
verses.9:29: and he spoke and disputed with the Hellenists; but they attempted to slay him.
verses.9:30: When the brethren learned of it, they brought him down to Caesarea and sent him away to Tarsus.
verses.9:31: So the church throughout all Judea, Galilee, and Samaria had peace and was built up; and walking in the fear of the Lord and in the comfort of the Holy Spirit, it was multiplied.
verses.9:32: Now it came to pass, as Peter journeyed through all those parts, that he came down also to the saints who dwelt in Lydda.
verses.9:33: There he found a certain man named Aeneas, who had lain on a pallet for eight years and was paralyzed.
verses.9:34: And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Arise and make your own bed." And immediately he arose.
verses.9:35: And all who dwelt in Lydda and Sharon saw him, and they turned to the Lord.
verses.9:36: Now in Joppa there was a certain disciple named Tabitha, which, translated, means Dorcas. This woman was full of good works and deeds of charity that she did.
verses.9:37: And it came to pass in those days that she fell ill and died; and having washed her, they laid her in an upper room.
verses.9:38: Now since Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, urging him, "Do not delay in coming to us."
verses.9:39: So Peter arose and went with them. When he had arrived, they led him up into the upper room, and all the widows stood beside him weeping and displaying the tunics and garments that Dorcas had made while she was with them.
verses.9:40: But Peter put them all outside, and kneeling down, he prayed; and turning toward the body, he said, "Tabitha, arise." And she opened her eyes, and when she saw Peter, she sat up.
verses.9:41: Then giving her his hand, he raised her up; and calling the saints and the widows, he presented her alive.
verses.9:42: And this became known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
verses.9:43: And it came to pass that he stayed many days in Joppa with a certain Simon, a tanner.
verses.10:1: Now a certain man in Caesarea named Cornelius, a centurion of the cohort called the Italian,
verses.10:2: a devout man and one who feared God with all his household, giving many alms to the people and praying to God continually,
verses.10:3: saw plainly in a vision, about the ninth hour of the day, an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, "Cornelius."
verses.10:4: And fixing his eyes on him, filled with fear, he said, "What is it, Lord?" And he said to him, "Your prayers and your alms have ascended as a memorial before God.
verses.10:5: And now send men to Joppa, and send for a certain Simon who is called Peter.
verses.10:6: He is lodging with a certain Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea."
verses.10:7: Now when the angel who had spoken to him departed, he summoned two of his household servants and a devout soldier from among those who waited on him continually,
verses.10:8: and having recounted all things to them, he sent them to Joppa.
verses.10:9: On the following day, as they were journeying and approaching the city, Peter went up upon the housetop to pray, about the sixth hour.
verses.10:10: And he became very hungry and wished to eat; yet while they were making preparation, a trance came upon him,
verses.10:11: and he beheld heaven opened, and a certain vessel descending like a great linen sheet, being lowered by four corners to the earth,
verses.10:12: in which were all kinds of four-footed animals and creeping things of the earth, and birds of heaven.
verses.10:13: And there came a voice to him, "Arise, Peter; slay and eat."
verses.10:14: But Peter replied, "By no means, Lord, for I have never eaten anything common and unclean."
verses.10:15: And a voice came to him again the second time, "What God has made clean, you shall not call common."
verses.10:16: Now this occurred three times, and immediately the vessel was taken up into heaven.
verses.10:17: Now while Peter was greatly perplexed within himself as to what the vision he had seen might signify, behold, the men sent by Cornelius, having inquired for Simon's house, stood at the gate,
verses.10:18: and calling out, they inquired whether Simon, who was called Peter, was lodging there.
verses.10:19: Now while Peter was pondering over the vision, the Spirit said to him, "Behold, men are seeking you.
verses.10:20: But arise, go down, and travel with them, doubting nothing at all, for I have sent them."
verses.10:21: So Peter went down to the men and said, "Behold, I am the one whom you seek. What is the cause for which you are here?"
verses.10:22: And they said, "Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man and one who fears God, well attested by the entire nation of the Jews, was divinely directed by a holy angel to send for you to his house and to hear words from you."
verses.10:23: Therefore he invited them in and lodged them. On the next day he arose and set out with them, and some of the brethren from Joppa went along with him.
verses.10:24: And on the following day he entered Caesarea. Now Cornelius was eagerly awaiting them, having gathered together his kinsmen and close friends.
verses.10:25: And when it came to pass that Peter entered, Cornelius met him, fell down at his feet, and worshiped him.
verses.10:26: But Peter raised him up, saying, "Arise; I myself am also a man."
verses.10:27: And as he conversed with him, he went inside and found many gathered together.
verses.10:28: And he said to them, "You yourselves know how unlawful it is for a Jewish man to join himself to or approach one of another nation; yet to me God has shown that I should not call any man common or unclean.
verses.10:29: Therefore I also came without objection when summoned. I inquire, then, for what reason you sent for me."
verses.10:30: And Cornelius said, "Four days ago, to this very hour, I was keeping the ninth hour of prayer in my house; and behold, a man stood before me in radiant apparel,
verses.10:31: and said, 'Cornelius, your prayer has been heard, and your alms have been remembered in the sight of God.
verses.10:32: Send therefore to Joppa and call for Simon, who is called Peter; he is lodging in the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea.'
verses.10:33: At once, therefore, I sent to you, and you have done well in coming. Now, then, we are all present in the sight of God to hear everything that has been commanded you by the Lord."
verses.10:34: Then Peter opened his mouth and said, "Truly I perceive that God is not one who shows partiality,
verses.10:35: but in every nation he who fears Him and practices righteousness is acceptable to Him.
verses.10:36: As for the word which He sent to the sons of Israel, proclaiming the good news of peace through Jesus Christ—He is Lord of all—
verses.10:37: you yourselves know the event that came to pass throughout all Judea, beginning from Galilee after the baptism which John proclaimed:
verses.10:38: Jesus of Nazareth—how God anointed Him with the Holy Spirit and with power, who passed through doing good and healing all those oppressed by the devil, because God was with Him.
verses.10:39: And we are witnesses of all the things He did both in the country of the Jews and in Jerusalem—whom they also slew, hanging Him on a tree.
verses.10:40: Him God raised up on the third day and granted that He should become manifest,
verses.10:41: not to all the people, but to witnesses appointed beforehand by God—to us, who ate and drank with Him after He rose from the dead.
verses.10:42: And He charged us to proclaim to the people, and to bear solemn witness that He is the One ordained by God to be Judge of the living and the dead.
verses.10:43: To Him all the prophets bear witness, that everyone who believes in Him shall receive remission of sins through His name."
verses.10:44: As Peter was still speaking these words, the Holy Spirit fell upon all who were hearing the word.
verses.10:45: And the believers from the circumcision, as many as had accompanied Peter, were amazed because upon the Gentiles also the gift of the Holy Spirit had been poured out;
verses.10:46: for they were hearing them speak in tongues and magnify God. Then Peter responded,
verses.10:47: "Can anyone withhold the water, that these should not be baptized, who have received the Holy Spirit even as we ourselves have?"
verses.10:48: And he commanded them to be baptized in the name of Jesus Christ. Then they asked him to remain for several days.
verses.11:1: Now the apostles and the brethren who were throughout Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
verses.11:2: And when Peter went up to Jerusalem, those of the circumcision disputed with him,
verses.11:3: saying, "You went in to men who were uncircumcised and ate with them."
verses.11:4: Then Peter began to set it forth to them in order, saying,
verses.11:5: "I was in the city of Joppa praying, and in a trance I saw a vision: a certain vessel coming down like a great sheet, lowered from heaven by four corners, and it came even to me.
verses.11:6: Gazing intently into it, I observed and saw the four-footed creatures of the earth, and the wild beasts, and the creeping things, and the birds of heaven.
verses.11:7: I also heard a voice saying to me, 'Arise, Peter; slay and eat.'
verses.11:8: But I replied, 'By no means, Lord! For nothing common or unclean has ever entered my mouth.'
verses.11:9: Yet a voice answered a second time from heaven, 'What God has made clean, you must not call common.'
verses.11:10: And this occurred three times, and all things were drawn up again into heaven.
verses.11:11: And behold, at that very moment three men stood at the house where we were, having been sent to me from Caesarea.
verses.11:12: And the Spirit told me to go with them, making no distinction. Moreover, these six brethren also accompanied me, and we entered the man's house.
verses.11:13: And he related to us how he had seen the angel standing in his house and saying, 'Send to Joppa and summon Simon who is called Peter,
verses.11:14: who will speak words to you by which you shall be saved—you and all your household.'
verses.11:15: And as I began to speak, the Holy Spirit fell upon them, just as He did upon us at the beginning.
verses.11:16: Then I recalled the word of the Lord, how He said, 'John indeed baptized with water, but you shall be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'
verses.11:17: Therefore, if God granted them the same gift as He did to us when we believed on the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I that I should be able to hinder God?"
verses.11:18: When they heard these things, they fell silent and glorified God, saying, "Then to the Gentiles also God has granted repentance leading to life."
verses.11:19: Now those who had been scattered because of the tribulation that arose over Stephen traveled as far as Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch, speaking the word to no one except Jews alone.
verses.11:20: Yet some of them were men from Cyprus and Cyrene, who, upon coming to Antioch, spoke to the Hellenists as well, proclaiming the good news of the Lord Jesus.
verses.11:21: And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a large number who believed turned to the Lord.
verses.11:22: Now the report concerning them came to the ears of the church that was in Jerusalem, and they sent forth Barnabas as far as Antioch.
verses.11:23: When he arrived and beheld the grace of God, he rejoiced and exhorted them all with purpose of heart to abide with the Lord,
verses.11:24: for he was a good man and full of the Holy Spirit and faith. And a considerable multitude was added to the Lord.
verses.11:25: Then he departed to Tarsus to search for Saul,
verses.11:26: and when he had found him, he brought him to Antioch. So it came to pass that for a whole year they assembled with the church and taught a considerable multitude; and in Antioch the disciples were first called Christians.
verses.11:27: Now during those days prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.
verses.11:28: And one of them named Agabus stood up and signified through the Spirit that a great famine was about to come upon the whole inhabited world, which indeed occurred under Claudius.
verses.11:29: Therefore the disciples, each according to his means, resolved to send relief to the brethren who dwelt in Judea;
verses.11:30: and this they also did, sending it to the elders by the hand of Barnabas and Saul.
verses.12:1: Now about that time King Herod stretched forth his hands to afflict some of those belonging to the church.
verses.12:2: And he slew James the brother of John with the sword.
verses.12:3: And seeing that this was pleasing to the Jews, he proceeded to arrest Peter as well (now these were the Days of Unleavened Bread).
verses.12:4: Having seized him, he cast him into prison, delivering him to four squads of four soldiers to guard him, intending after the Passover to bring him forth before the people.
verses.12:5: So Peter was kept in the prison, yet fervent prayer was continually being made to God by the church on his behalf.
verses.12:6: Now when Herod was about to bring him out, on that very night Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, bound with two chains, while sentries before the door were guarding the prison.
verses.12:7: And behold, an angel of the Lord stood beside him, and a light shone in the cell; and striking Peter on the side, he woke him, saying, "Arise quickly!" And his chains fell off from his hands.
verses.12:8: Then the angel said to him, "Gird yourself and fasten on your sandals." And he did so. Then he said to him, "Wrap your cloak around you and follow me."
verses.12:9: So he went out and followed, not knowing that what was being done through the angel was real, but supposing he was seeing a vision.
verses.12:10: When they had passed the first guard post and the second, they came to the iron gate that leads into the city, which opened for them of its own accord; and going out, they proceeded down one street, and at once the angel departed from him.
verses.12:11: And when Peter came to himself, he said, "Now I truly know that the Lord has sent forth His angel and delivered me from the hand of Herod and from all the expectation of the people of the Jews."
verses.12:12: Realizing this, he came to the house of Mary, the mother of John whose surname was Mark, where many were assembled together and praying.
verses.12:13: And when he knocked at the door of the outer gate, a servant girl named Rhoda came to answer.
verses.12:14: Recognizing Peter's voice, in her joy she did not open the gate, but ran inside and reported that Peter was standing before the gate.
verses.12:15: But they said to her, "You are out of your mind!" Yet she firmly insisted that it was indeed so. Then they said, "It is his angel."
verses.12:16: Meanwhile Peter kept on knocking; and when they opened it, they saw him and were astonished.
verses.12:17: Motioning to them with his hand to be silent, he recounted to them how the Lord had led him out of the prison, and he said, "Report these things to James and to the brethren." Then he went out and departed for another place.
verses.12:18: Now when daylight came, there was no small commotion among the soldiers concerning what had become of Peter.
verses.12:19: And when Herod had searched for him and did not find him, he examined the guards and ordered them to be led away to execution. Then he went down from Judea to Caesarea and stayed there.
verses.12:20: Now he was fiercely angry with the people of Tyre and Sidon; yet they came before him with one accord, and having won over Blastus, the king's chamberlain, they sought peace, because their country was nourished from the king's territory.
verses.12:21: So on an appointed day Herod arrayed himself in royal apparel, took his seat upon the tribunal, and delivered an address to them.
verses.12:22: And the populace kept shouting, "The voice of a god, and not of a man!"
verses.12:23: At once an angel of the Lord struck him, because he did not give the glory to God; and he was eaten by worms and breathed his last.
verses.12:24: But the word of God kept increasing and multiplying.
verses.12:25: Now Barnabas and Saul returned, having fulfilled their ministry to Jerusalem, taking along with them John who was called Mark.
verses.13:1: Now there were in Antioch, in the church that was there, prophets and teachers: Barnabas, Simeon who was called Niger, Lucius the Cyrenian, Manaen who had been raised alongside Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
verses.13:2: As they were ministering to the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Set apart now for Me Barnabas and Saul for the work to which I have called them."
verses.13:3: Then, having fasted and prayed and laid hands upon them, they sent them forth.
verses.13:4: So these men, being sent forth by the Holy Spirit, went down to Seleucia, and from there they sailed away to Cyprus.
verses.13:5: And when they arrived at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews; and they also had John as their attendant.
verses.13:6: When they had passed through the whole island as far as Paphos, they found a certain sorcerer, a Jewish false prophet, whose name was Bar-Jesus,
verses.13:7: who was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding. This man summoned Barnabas and Saul and earnestly sought to hear the word of God.
verses.13:8: Yet Elymas the sorcerer—for so his name is translated—withstood them, seeking to turn the proconsul away from the faith.
verses.13:9: Then Saul, who is also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, fixed his eyes intently upon him
verses.13:10: and said, "O you who are full of all deceit and all villainy, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness, will you not cease perverting the straight paths of the Lord?
verses.13:11: And now, behold, the hand of the Lord is upon you, and you shall be blind, not seeing the sun for a season." At once a mist and darkness fell upon him, and wandering about, he sought those who would lead him by the hand.
verses.13:12: Then the proconsul, seeing what had taken place, believed, being astonished at the teaching of the Lord.
verses.13:13: Now Paul and his companions set sail from Paphos and came to Perga in Pamphylia; yet John departed from them and returned to Jerusalem.
verses.13:14: Going on from Perga, they came to Pisidian Antioch, and entering the synagogue on the Sabbath day, they sat down.
verses.13:15: After the reading of the Law and the Prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent word to them, saying, "Men and brethren, if there is any word of exhortation among you for the people, speak."
verses.13:16: Then Paul rose up, and motioning with his hand, he said, "Men of Israel, and you who fear God, listen.
verses.13:17: The God of this people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people during their sojourn in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm He brought them out of it.
verses.13:18: And for a period of about forty years He bore with their ways in the wilderness.
verses.13:19: And when He had overthrown seven nations in the land of Canaan, He allotted their land to them as an inheritance,
verses.13:20: which took about four hundred and fifty years. And after these things He gave them judges until Samuel the prophet.
verses.13:21: And afterward they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul the son of Kish, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, for forty years.
verses.13:22: And when He had removed him, He raised up David for them as king, of whom He also testified and said, 'I have found David the son of Jesse, a man after My own heart, who will carry out all My will.'
verses.13:23: From the seed of this man, according to promise, God brought to Israel a Savior, Jesus,
verses.13:24: after John had first proclaimed, before His coming, a baptism of repentance to all the people of Israel.
verses.13:25: And as John was completing his course, he said, 'What do you suppose me to be? I am not He. Yet behold, One is coming after me, the sandal of whose feet I am not worthy to untie.'
verses.13:26: Men and brethren, sons of the family of Abraham, and those among you who fear God, to us the word of this salvation has been sent forth.
verses.13:27: For those who dwell in Jerusalem and their rulers, because they did not recognize Him nor the voices of the prophets that are read every Sabbath, fulfilled them in condemning Him.
verses.13:28: And though they found no cause for death, they asked Pilate that He should be put to death.
verses.13:29: Now when they had carried out all that was written concerning Him, they took Him down from the tree and laid Him in a tomb.
verses.13:30: Yet God raised Him from the dead,
verses.13:31: and for many days He appeared to those who had gone up with Him from Galilee to Jerusalem, who are now His witnesses to the people.
verses.13:32: And we bring you the good tidings of the promise made to the fathers,
verses.13:33: that God has fulfilled this very promise for our children by raising up Jesus, as it is also written in the second Psalm: 'You are My Son; this day I have begotten You.'
verses.13:34: And concerning the fact that He raised Him from the dead, no more to return to corruption, He has spoken thus: 'I will give you the faithful and holy mercies of David.'
verses.13:35: Therefore He also says in another Psalm: 'You will not permit Your Holy One to see corruption.'
verses.13:36: For David, after he had served the purpose of God in his own generation, fell asleep, was gathered to his fathers, and saw corruption;
verses.13:37: yet He whom God raised up did not see corruption.
verses.13:38: Let it be known to you, therefore, men and brethren, that through Him forgiveness of sins is proclaimed to you, and from all things from which you could not be justified by the law of Moses,
verses.13:39: in Him everyone who believes is justified.
verses.13:40: Take heed, therefore, lest what has been spoken in the Prophets come upon you:
verses.13:41: 'Behold, you scoffers, marvel and perish; for I am working a deed in your days, a deed which you will by no means believe, even if someone recounts it to you.'"
verses.13:42: As they were going out, the people pleaded that these words be spoken to them on the next Sabbath.
verses.13:43: Now when the assembly of the synagogue was dismissed, many of the Jews and devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who, speaking with them, urged them to abide in the grace of God.
verses.13:44: On the next Sabbath almost the whole city gathered together to hear the word of God.
verses.13:45: Yet when the Jews saw the multitudes, they were filled with jealousy and contradicted the things spoken by Paul, blaspheming.
verses.13:46: Then Paul and Barnabas spoke out boldly and said, "It was necessary that the word of God should be spoken to you first; yet since you thrust it away and judge yourselves unworthy of everlasting life, behold, we turn to the Gentiles.
verses.13:47: For so the Lord has commanded us: 'I have appointed you as a light for the Gentiles, that you should be for salvation to the farthest end of the earth.'"
verses.13:48: Now when the Gentiles heard this, they rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord; and as many as had been appointed to eternal life believed.
verses.13:49: And the word of the Lord was being spread abroad throughout all that region.
verses.13:50: Yet the Jews incited the devout women of high standing and the leading men of the city, and stirred up persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and cast them out from their borders.
verses.13:51: So they shook off the dust of their feet against them and came to Iconium.
verses.13:52: And the disciples were continually filled with joy and with the Holy Spirit.
verses.14:1: Now it came to pass in Iconium that they entered together into the synagogue of the Jews, and spoke in such a manner that a great multitude of both Jews and Greeks believed.
verses.14:2: But the Jews who refused to believe stirred up and embittered the souls of the Gentiles against the brethren.
verses.14:3: Therefore they stayed a considerable time, speaking boldly in the Lord, who bore witness to the word of His grace, granting signs and wonders to be done through their hands.
verses.14:4: But the multitude of the city was divided; some stood with the Jews, and others with the apostles.
verses.14:5: And when a violent attempt was made by both the Gentiles and the Jews, together with their rulers, to mistreat and stone them,
verses.14:6: they became aware of it and fled to the cities of Lycaonia—Lystra and Derbe—and to the surrounding region,
verses.14:7: and there they continued proclaiming the gospel.
verses.14:8: Now in Lystra a certain man sat who had no strength in his feet, lame from his mother's womb, who had never walked.
verses.14:9: This man listened to Paul speaking; and Paul, gazing intently at him and perceiving that he had faith to be made well,
verses.14:10: said with a loud voice, "Stand upright upon your feet!" And he leaped up and began to walk.
verses.14:11: When the crowds saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voices, saying in the Lycaonian tongue, "The gods have become like men and have come down to us!"
verses.14:12: And they called Barnabas Zeus, and Paul Hermes, because he was the chief speaker.
verses.14:13: Then the priest of Zeus, whose temple stood before the city, brought oxen and garlands to the gates and desired to offer sacrifice along with the crowds.
verses.14:14: But when the apostles Barnabas and Paul heard of it, they tore their garments and rushed out into the crowd, crying aloud
verses.14:15: and saying, "Men, why are you doing these things? We also are men of the same nature as you, bringing you good news that you should turn from these vain things to the living God, who made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them,
verses.14:16: who in bygone generations allowed all the nations to walk in their own ways.
verses.14:17: Yet He did not leave Himself without witness, for He did good, giving you rains from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling your hearts with food and gladness."
verses.14:18: Even by saying these words, they scarcely restrained the crowds from offering sacrifice to them.
verses.14:19: Then Jews arrived from Antioch and Iconium, and having won over the crowds, they stoned Paul and dragged him outside the city, supposing him to be dead.
verses.14:20: However, when the disciples gathered around him, he rose up and went into the city. And on the next day he departed with Barnabas for Derbe.
verses.14:21: After they had proclaimed the gospel to that city and made many disciples, they returned to Lystra, to Iconium, and to Antioch,
verses.14:22: strengthening the souls of the disciples, exhorting them to continue in the faith, and saying that through many tribulations we must enter into the kingdom of God.
verses.14:23: And when they had appointed elders for them in every church, and had prayed with fasting, they commended them to the Lord in whom they had believed.
verses.14:24: Then, having passed through Pisidia, they came to Pamphylia.
verses.14:25: And when they had spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia.
verses.14:26: From there they sailed away to Antioch, where they had been commended to the grace of God for the work which they had fulfilled.
verses.14:27: Now when they had arrived and gathered the church together, they reported all that God had done with them, and how He had opened a door of faith to the Gentiles.
verses.14:28: And they remained no little time with the disciples.
verses.15:1: Now certain men came down from Judea and were teaching the brethren, "Unless you are circumcised according to the custom of Moses, you cannot be saved."
verses.15:2: When therefore Paul and Barnabas had no small dissension and debate with them, they appointed Paul and Barnabas and certain others of their number to go up to Jerusalem to the apostles and elders concerning this question.
verses.15:3: So, being sent on their way by the church, they passed through both Phoenicia and Samaria, recounting in detail the conversion of the Gentiles; and they brought great joy to all the brethren.
verses.15:4: When they arrived in Jerusalem, they were welcomed by the church and the apostles and the elders, and they declared all that God had done with them.
verses.15:5: But some of the sect of the Pharisees who had believed rose up, saying, "It is necessary to circumcise them and to command them to keep the law of Moses."
verses.15:6: Then the apostles and the elders gathered together to consider this matter.
verses.15:7: And after there had been much debate, Peter stood up and said to them, "Men and brethren, you know that from early days God made choice among you, that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of the gospel and believe.
verses.15:8: And God, who knows the heart, bore witness to them by giving them the Holy Spirit, just as He also did to us,
verses.15:9: and made no distinction between us and them, cleansing their hearts by faith.
verses.15:10: Now therefore, why do you test God by placing a yoke upon the neck of the disciples which neither our fathers nor we were able to bear?
verses.15:11: Rather, we believe that through the grace of the Lord Jesus we shall be saved, in the very same manner as they."
verses.15:12: Then all the multitude fell silent and listened to Barnabas and Paul as they related all the signs and wonders God had worked among the Gentiles through them.
verses.15:13: And after they had fallen silent, James answered, saying, "Men and brethren, listen to me.
verses.15:14: Simeon has declared how God first visited the Gentiles to take from them a people for His name.
verses.15:15: And with this the words of the prophets agree, just as it is written:
verses.15:16: 'After these things I will return and will rebuild the tabernacle of David, which has fallen; and its ruins I will rebuild, and I will restore it,
verses.15:17: so that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord, even all the Gentiles upon whom My name has been called, says the Lord, who makes these things
verses.15:19: Therefore it is my judgment that we should not trouble those from among the Gentiles who are turning to God,
verses.15:20: but that we write to them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, from sexual immorality, from what is strangled, and from blood.
verses.15:21: For Moses has had from ancient generations those who preach him in every city, being read in the synagogues every Sabbath."
verses.15:22: Then it seemed good to the apostles and the elders, together with the whole church, to choose men from among themselves and send them to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas—namely, Judas called Barsabbas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren—
verses.15:23: writing by their hand: "The apostles and the elders, your brethren, to the brethren who are of the Gentiles in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Greetings.
verses.15:24: Since we have heard that some who went out from us have troubled you with words, unsettling your souls—though we gave them no command—
verses.15:25: it seemed good to us, having come to one accord, to choose men and send them to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
verses.15:26: men who have risked their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.15:27: We have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who will themselves also tell you the same things by word of mouth.
verses.15:28: For it has seemed good to the Holy Spirit and to us to lay upon you no greater burden than these necessary things:
verses.15:29: that you abstain from things sacrificed to idols, from blood, from things strangled, and from sexual immorality. If you keep yourselves from these, you will do well. Farewell."
verses.15:30: So when they were sent off, they went down to Antioch; and having gathered the multitude together, they delivered the letter.
verses.15:31: When they had read it, they rejoiced over its encouragement.
verses.15:32: Now Judas and Silas, being prophets themselves also, exhorted and strengthened the brethren with many words.
verses.15:33: And after they had spent some time, they were sent off in peace from the brethren to those who had sent them.
verses.15:35: But Paul and Barnabas remained in Antioch, teaching and preaching the word of the Lord, along with many others as well.
verses.15:36: Now after some days Paul said to Barnabas, "Let us return and visit the brethren in every city in which we proclaimed the word of the Lord, and see how they are faring."
verses.15:37: Now Barnabas wanted to take along with them John, who was called Mark.
verses.15:38: But Paul thought it best not to take along with them the one who had withdrawn from them in Pamphylia and had not gone with them to the work.
verses.15:39: And there arose such a sharp disagreement that they parted from one another; and Barnabas took Mark and sailed away to Cyprus,
verses.15:40: while Paul chose Silas and departed, having been commended by the brethren to the grace of the Lord.
verses.15:41: And he passed through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches.
verses.16:1: Now he arrived also at Derbe and at Lystra. And behold, there was a certain disciple there named Timothy, the son of a believing Jewish woman, yet of a Greek father,
verses.16:2: who received a good testimony from the brethren in Lystra and Iconium.
verses.16:3: Paul desired that this man go forth with him; and taking him, he circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for all of them knew that his father was a Greek.
verses.16:4: And as they journeyed through the cities, they delivered to them the decrees to observe, which had been decided by the apostles and elders who were in Jerusalem.
verses.16:5: Thus the churches were strengthened in the faith and abounded in number day by day.
verses.16:6: Now they went through the Phrygian and Galatian region, having been forbidden by the Holy Spirit to speak the word in Asia;
verses.16:7: and having come up to Mysia, they attempted to journey into Bithynia, yet the Spirit of Jesus did not allow them.
verses.16:8: Then, passing by Mysia, they descended to Troas.
verses.16:9: And a vision appeared to Paul during the night: a certain Macedonian man stood appealing to him and saying, "Cross over into Macedonia and help us."
verses.16:10: And when he had seen the vision, at once we sought to depart for Macedonia, concluding that God had called us to proclaim the gospel to them.
verses.16:11: Therefore, putting out to sea from Troas, we sailed a straight course to Samothrace, and on the following day to Neapolis,
verses.16:12: and from there to Philippi, which is a foremost city of that district of Macedonia, a colony. And we remained in this city for some days.
verses.16:13: And on the Sabbath day we went outside the gate beside a river, where we supposed there was a place of prayer; and sitting down, we spoke to the women who had gathered together.
verses.16:14: And a certain woman by the name of Lydia, a seller of purple from the city of Thyatira, a worshiper of God, was listening, whose heart the Lord opened to give heed to the things spoken by Paul.
verses.16:15: And when she had been baptized, along with her household, she appealed to us, saying, "If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord, enter into my house and abide." And she prevailed upon us.
verses.16:16: And it came to pass, as we were going to the place of prayer, that a certain young slave girl with a spirit of divination met us, who brought great profit to her masters by fortune-telling.
