verses.16:17: Following closely after Paul and us, she cried out, saying, "These men are bondservants of the Most High God, who declare to you a way of salvation."
verses.16:18: And she kept doing this for many days. But Paul, being greatly grieved, turned and said to the spirit, "I charge you in the name of Jesus Christ to come out from her." And it departed that very hour.
verses.16:19: But when her masters saw that the hope of their profit had departed, seizing Paul and Silas, they dragged them into the marketplace before the rulers,
verses.16:20: and having brought them before the magistrates, they said, "These men are throwing our city into turmoil, being Jews,
verses.16:21: and they proclaim customs that are not lawful for us to accept or to practice, since we are Romans."
verses.16:22: And the multitude rose up together against them; and the magistrates tore off their garments and ordered them to be beaten with rods.
verses.16:23: And having laid many lashes upon them, they cast them into prison, charging the jailer to guard them securely;
verses.16:24: who, having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison and secured their feet in the stocks.
verses.16:25: Now about midnight, as they prayed, Paul and Silas were singing hymns to God, and the prisoners were listening attentively to them.
verses.16:26: And suddenly a great earthquake took place, so that the foundations of the prison house were shaken; and instantly all the doors were opened, and the bonds of all were unfastened.
verses.16:27: And the jailer, having awakened from sleep and seeing the doors of the prison standing open, drew his sword and was about to slay himself, supposing that the prisoners had fled.
verses.16:28: But Paul called out in a loud voice, saying, "Do no harm to yourself, for all of us are here."
verses.16:29: Then he asked for lights and rushed inside, and trembling, he fell down before Paul and Silas;
verses.16:30: and having brought them outside, he said, "Sirs, what must I do that I may be saved?"
verses.16:31: And they said, "Believe upon the Lord Jesus, and you shall be saved—you and your household."
verses.16:32: And they spoke the word of the Lord to him, together with all those who were in his house.
verses.16:33: And taking them in that very hour of the night, he washed their wounds; and at once he himself and all his own were baptized.
verses.16:34: And bringing them up into his house, he set a table before them and rejoiced greatly with his entire household, having believed in God.
verses.16:35: Now when day broke, the magistrates sent the officers, saying, "Release those men."
verses.16:36: And the jailer reported these words to Paul: "The magistrates have sent word that you should be released. Now therefore, come forth and go in peace."
verses.16:37: But Paul said to them, "Having beaten us publicly, uncondemned—men who are Romans—they cast us into prison; and now are they casting us out secretly? Certainly not! Rather, let them come themselves and lead us out."
verses.16:38: Then the officers reported these words to the magistrates, and they became afraid when they heard that they were Romans;
verses.16:39: and coming, they apologized to them; and having led them out, they asked them to depart from the city.
verses.16:40: And coming forth from the prison, they went to Lydia's house; and having seen the brethren, they encouraged them and departed.
verses.17:1: Now after traveling through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:2: And according to his custom, Paul went in among them, and for three Sabbaths he reasoned with them from the Scriptures,
verses.17:3: opening and setting forth that it was necessary for the Christ to suffer and to rise from the dead, and declaring, "This is the Christ—Jesus, whom I proclaim to you."
verses.17:4: And some of them were persuaded and joined Paul and Silas, along with a great multitude of the devout Greeks and not a few of the prominent women.
verses.17:5: But the Jews, becoming filled with jealousy, took along some wicked men from the marketplace, and forming a mob, they threw the city into an uproar; and attacking the house of Jason, they sought to bring them out to the public assembly.
verses.17:6: Yet when they did not find them, they dragged Jason and certain brethren before the city magistrates, crying out, "These men who have turned the world upside down have arrived here as well,
verses.17:7: whom Jason has received into his house; and all of these act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, proclaiming that there is another king—Jesus."
verses.17:8: And they troubled the multitude and the city magistrates when they heard these things.
verses.17:9: And after taking security from Jason and the rest, they released them.
verses.17:10: Then the brethren immediately sent Paul and Silas away by night to Berea; and upon arriving there, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.
verses.17:11: Now these were more noble-minded than those in Thessalonica, for they received the word with all eagerness, examining the Scriptures day by day to see whether these things were so.
verses.17:12: Therefore many of them believed, as well as not a few of the prominent Greek women and men.
verses.17:13: But when the Jews from Thessalonica learned that the word of God had been proclaimed by Paul in Berea also, they came there as well, agitating and troubling the multitudes.
verses.17:14: Then the brethren immediately sent Paul off to go as far as the sea, while both Silas and Timothy remained there.
verses.17:15: And those who escorted Paul brought him as far as Athens; and having received a command for Silas and Timothy to come to him with all speed, they departed.
verses.17:16: Now while Paul was waiting for them in Athens, his spirit was greatly provoked within him as he beheld that the city was full of idols.
verses.17:17: Therefore he reasoned in the synagogue with the Jews and with the devout worshipers, and in the marketplace every day with those who happened to be there.
verses.17:18: And certain of the Epicurean and Stoic philosophers also engaged him in discussion; and some said, "What might this babbler wish to say?" Others said, "He seems to be a proclaimer of foreign deities," because he was proclaiming the gospel of Jesus and the resurrection.
verses.17:19: And taking hold of him, they brought him to the Areopagus, saying, "May we know what this new teaching is that is spoken by you?
verses.17:20: For you are bringing certain strange things to our ears; therefore we wish to know what these things mean."
verses.17:21: Now all the Athenians and the foreigners who resided there spent their leisure in nothing else but either to speak or to hear something new.
verses.17:22: Then Paul stood in the midst of the Areopagus and said, "Men of Athens, I perceive that in all respects you are exceedingly religious;
verses.17:23: for as I passed along and carefully observed the objects of your worship, I even found an altar upon which was inscribed, 'To an Unknown God.' Therefore what you worship in ignorance, this I proclaim to you.
verses.17:24: The God who made the world and everything that is in it, since He is Lord of heaven and earth, does not dwell in temples made with hands,
verses.17:25: nor is He served by human hands, as though He needed anything, since He Himself gives to all life, breath, and all things.
verses.17:26: And from one man He made every nation of mankind to dwell upon all the face of the earth, having determined their appointed seasons and the boundaries of their habitation,
verses.17:27: that they should seek God, in the hope that they might reach out for Him and find Him, though indeed He is not far from each one of us.
verses.17:28: For in Him we live and move and exist, as even some of your own poets have spoken, 'For we also are His offspring.'
verses.17:29: Therefore, being the offspring of God, we ought not to suppose that the Divine Being is like gold or silver or stone, an image formed by the craft and imagination of man.
verses.17:30: Having overlooked these times of ignorance, God now declares to men that all people everywhere should repent,
verses.17:31: because He has fixed a day on which He is going to judge the world in righteousness by a Man whom He has appointed, having furnished assurance to all by raising Him from the dead."
verses.17:32: Now when they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some mocked, while others said, "We will hear you again concerning this matter."
verses.17:33: So Paul went out from their midst.
verses.17:34: Yet certain men joined him and believed, among whom were Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and others with them.
verses.18:1: After these things he departed from Athens and came to Corinth.
verses.18:2: And finding a certain Jew named Aquila, a native of Pontus, who had recently arrived from Italy with his wife Priscilla—because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart from Rome—he went to them.
verses.18:3: And because he was of the same trade, he stayed with them and they worked together, for by trade they were tentmakers.
verses.18:4: And he reasoned in the synagogue every Sabbath, and sought to persuade both Jews and Greeks.
verses.18:5: Now when both Silas and Timothy had come down from Macedonia, Paul was wholly occupied with the word, solemnly testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.18:6: But when they opposed him and spoke blasphemy, he shook out his garments and said to them, "Your blood be upon your own heads! I am innocent; from now on I shall go to the Gentiles."
verses.18:7: And departing from there, he entered the house of a certain man named Titius Justus, one who worshiped God, whose house adjoined the synagogue.
verses.18:8: Then Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, believed in the Lord together with his entire household; and many of the Corinthians, as they heard, believed and were baptized.
verses.18:9: And the Lord spoke to Paul by night in a vision, "Do not be afraid, but speak, and do not keep silent,
verses.18:10: for I am with you, and no one shall attack you to do you harm; for I have many people in this city."
verses.18:11: And he stayed there a year and six months, teaching the word of God among them.
verses.18:12: Now when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews rose up with one accord against Paul and brought him before the judgment seat,
verses.18:13: saying, "This man is persuading people to worship God contrary to the law."
verses.18:14: But as Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, "If indeed it were a matter of some wrongdoing or wicked crime, O Jews, I would rightly bear with you;
verses.18:15: but since these are questions concerning words and names and your own law, see to it yourselves; I have no desire to be a judge of such matters."
verses.18:16: And he drove them away from the judgment seat.
verses.18:17: Then they all seized Sosthenes, the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him in front of the judgment seat; yet Gallio paid no regard to any of these things.
verses.18:18: Now Paul, after remaining yet many days, took leave of the brethren and set sail for Syria, accompanied by Priscilla and Aquila, having had his hair cut short at Cenchreae, for he had taken a vow.
verses.18:19: And they arrived at Ephesus, where he left them behind; yet he himself entered the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews.
verses.18:20: When they asked him to remain for a longer time, he did not consent,
verses.18:21: but taking leave of them and saying, "I shall return to you again, if God wills," he set sail from Ephesus.
verses.18:22: And having landed at Caesarea, he went up and greeted the church, and then went down to Antioch.
verses.18:23: After spending some time there, he departed and passed through the region of Galatia and Phrygia in order, strengthening all the disciples.
verses.18:24: Now a certain Jew named Apollos, an Alexandrian by birth, an eloquent man, arrived at Ephesus, being mighty in the Scriptures.
verses.18:25: This man had been instructed in the way of the Lord; and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and taught accurately the things concerning Jesus, though he knew only the baptism of John.
verses.18:26: And he began to speak boldly in the synagogue; but when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they took him aside and explained to him the way of God more accurately.
verses.18:27: Now when he wished to cross over to Achaia, the brethren encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to welcome him; and upon arriving, he greatly helped those who had believed through grace,
verses.18:28: for he vigorously refuted the Jews in public, demonstrating through the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.
verses.19:1: Now it came to pass, while Apollos was in Corinth, that Paul, after passing through the upper regions, came to Ephesus and found certain disciples.
verses.19:2: And he said to them, "Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?" And they answered him, "No, we have not even heard whether there is a Holy Spirit."
verses.19:3: And he said, "Into what then were you baptized?" And they replied, "Into the baptism of John."
verses.19:4: Then Paul said, "John baptized with a baptism of repentance, telling the people that they should believe in the One coming after him, that is, in Jesus."
verses.19:5: And when they heard this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.
verses.19:6: And when Paul laid hands upon them, the Holy Spirit came upon them, and they began speaking in tongues and prophesying.
verses.19:7: And there were about twelve men in all.
verses.19:8: Now he entered the synagogue and spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading concerning the kingdom of God.
verses.19:9: But when some became hardened and refused to believe, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the lecture hall of Tyrannus.
verses.19:10: This went on for two years, so that all who dwelt in Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the word of the Lord.
verses.19:11: Now God was working miracles of no ordinary kind through the hands of Paul,
verses.19:12: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.
verses.19:13: Then some of the itinerant Jewish exorcists also undertook to invoke the name of the Lord Jesus over those who had evil spirits, saying, "I adjure you by the Jesus whom Paul proclaims."
verses.19:14: Now seven sons of a certain Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.
verses.19:15: And the evil spirit answered and said to them, "Jesus I know, and Paul I recognize, but who are you?"
verses.19:16: Then the man in whom the evil spirit was sprang upon them, mastered all of them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled from that house naked and wounded.
verses.19:17: And this became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who dwelt in Ephesus; and fear fell upon all of them, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
verses.19:18: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing and disclosing their practices.
verses.19:19: And a great number of those who had practiced magic arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all; and they counted the value of them and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.
verses.19:20: In this way the word of the Lord increased mightily and prevailed.
verses.19:21: Now after these things were completed, Paul resolved in the Spirit to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying, "After I have been there, I must see Rome as well."
verses.19:22: So having sent into Macedonia two of those who ministered to him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed on in Asia for a while.
verses.19:23: Now about that time no small commotion arose concerning the Way.
verses.19:24: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no small business to the craftsmen.
verses.19:25: He assembled them, together with the workmen of similar occupations, and said, "Men, you know that from this trade we have our prosperity,
verses.19:26: and you see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but throughout almost all of Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away a great multitude, saying that gods made with hands are not gods.
verses.19:27: And not only is this trade of ours in danger of falling into disrepute, but also the temple of the great goddess Artemis may be counted as nothing, and she whom all Asia and the world worship may even be deposed from her majesty."
verses.19:28: When they heard this, they became full of wrath and kept crying out, saying, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:29: So the city was filled with confusion, and with one accord they rushed into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonians who were Paul's traveling companions.
verses.19:30: Now when Paul desired to go in among the people, the disciples would not permit him.
verses.19:31: And some of the Asiarchs also, who were his friends, sent word to him, urging him not to venture into the theater.
verses.19:32: Meanwhile some were shouting one thing and some another, for the assembly was in confusion, and the greater part did not know for what reason they had come together.
verses.19:33: Then some of the crowd prompted Alexander, whom the Jews had put forward; and Alexander motioned with his hand and wished to make a defense before the people.
verses.19:34: But when they recognized that he was a Jew, one voice arose from them all as they cried out for about two hours, "Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!"
verses.19:35: When the town clerk had quieted the crowd, he said, "Men of Ephesus, what man is there who does not know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great Artemis and of the image that fell from heaven?
verses.19:36: Therefore, since these things cannot be contradicted, you ought to keep calm and do nothing rash.
verses.19:37: For you have brought these men here, though they are neither temple robbers nor blasphemers of our goddess.
verses.19:38: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen with him have a complaint against anyone, the courts are open and there are proconsuls; let them bring charges against one another.
verses.19:39: But if you seek anything concerning other matters, it shall be settled in the lawful assembly.
verses.19:40: For indeed we are in danger of being charged with rioting over today's events, since there is no cause, and we shall not be able to give an account for this disorderly gathering." And after saying these things, he dismissed the assembly.
verses.20:1: Now after the tumult had ceased, Paul summoned the disciples, and having exhorted them, he took leave of them and departed to go into Macedonia.
verses.20:2: And having passed through those regions and encouraged them with many words, he came into Greece,
verses.20:3: and spent three months there. And when a plot was laid against him by the Jews as he was about to set sail for Syria, he purposed to return by way of Macedonia.
verses.20:4: And there accompanied him Sopater the son of Pyrrhus, of Berea; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gaius of Derbe, and Timothy; and of Asia, Tychicus and Trophimus.
verses.20:5: Now these, having arrived, were waiting for us at Troas.
verses.20:6: But we sailed away from Philippi after the Days of Unleavened Bread, and within five days we came to them at Troas, where we remained seven days.
verses.20:7: Now on the first day of the week, when we were gathered together to break bread, Paul discoursed with them, intending to depart the next day, and he prolonged his speech until midnight.
verses.20:8: And there were many lamps in the upper room where we were assembled.
verses.20:9: And a certain young man named Eutychus was sitting in the window, sinking into a deep sleep as Paul continued speaking at great length; and being overcome by sleep, he fell down from the third story and was lifted up dead.
verses.20:10: But Paul went down, fell upon him, and embracing him, said, "Do not be alarmed, for his life is in him."
verses.20:11: Then when he had gone up again, and had broken the bread and eaten, and had conversed a long while, even until daybreak, he so departed.
verses.20:12: And they brought the lad alive, and they were comforted in no small measure.
verses.20:13: Now we went ahead to the ship and set sail for Assos, intending to take Paul aboard from there; for so he had arranged, intending himself to travel on foot.
verses.20:14: And when he met us at Assos, we took him aboard and came to Mitylene.
verses.20:15: And sailing away from there, on the following day we arrived opposite Chios; and the next day we put in at Samos; and on the day after that we came to Miletus.
verses.20:16: For Paul had decided to sail past Ephesus, so that he might not have to spend time in Asia; for he was hastening to be in Jerusalem, if it were possible for him, on the Day of Pentecost.
verses.20:17: Now from Miletus he sent to Ephesus and summoned the elders of the church.
verses.20:18: And when they had come to him, he said to them, "You yourselves know, from the first day that I set foot in Asia, in what manner I lived among you the whole time,
verses.20:19: serving the Lord with all humility, and with tears and trials that befell me through the plots of the Jews;
verses.20:20: how I withheld nothing that was profitable, but proclaimed it to you and taught you publicly and from house to house,
verses.20:21: solemnly testifying both to Jews and to Greeks of repentance toward God and faith in our Lord Jesus.
verses.20:22: And now, behold, bound in the spirit, I am going to Jerusalem, not knowing the things that shall meet me there,
verses.20:23: except that the Holy Spirit solemnly testifies to me in every city, saying that bonds and afflictions await me.
verses.20:24: Yet I do not count my life of any worth as precious to myself, if only I may complete my course and the ministry that I received from the Lord Jesus, to testify solemnly to the gospel of the grace of God.
verses.20:25: And now, behold, I know that all of you, among whom I have gone about proclaiming the kingdom, shall see my face no more.
verses.20:26: Therefore I testify to you on this very day that I am guiltless of the blood of all,
verses.20:27: for I did not hold back from proclaiming to you the whole counsel of God.
verses.20:28: Keep watch over yourselves and over all the flock, in which the Holy Spirit has appointed you overseers, to shepherd the church of God, which He acquired through His own blood.
verses.20:29: I know that after my departure fierce wolves shall come in among you, not sparing the flock;
verses.20:30: and from among your own selves men shall arise speaking perverse things, to draw away the disciples after themselves.
verses.20:31: Therefore be watchful, remembering that for three years, night and day, I did not cease to admonish each one with tears.
verses.20:32: And now I entrust you to God and to the word of His grace, which has power to build you up and to grant the inheritance among all who have been sanctified.
verses.20:33: I have coveted no one's silver or gold or apparel.
verses.20:34: You yourselves know that these hands have ministered to my own needs and to those who were with me.
verses.20:35: In all things I have shown you that by laboring in this manner we must support the weak, and remember the words of the Lord Jesus, how He Himself said, 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.'"
verses.20:36: And when he had spoken these things, he knelt down and prayed with them all.
verses.20:37: And there was great weeping among them all, and falling upon Paul's neck, they kissed him again and again,
verses.20:38: grieving most of all over the word he had spoken, that they would behold his face no more. And they accompanied him to the ship.
verses.21:1: Now when it came to pass that we had torn ourselves away from them and put out to sea, we ran a straight course and came to Cos, and on the following day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.
verses.21:2: And finding a ship crossing over to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
verses.21:3: When we had sighted Cyprus and left it on the left, we sailed on to Syria and landed at Tyre, for there the ship was to unload its cargo.
verses.21:4: Having sought out the disciples, we remained there seven days; and through the Spirit they kept telling Paul not to set foot in Jerusalem.
verses.21:5: When we had completed those days, we departed and went on our way, while all of them, with wives and children, escorted us until we were outside the city; and kneeling down on the shore, we prayed,
verses.21:6: and said farewell to one another. Then we went aboard the ship, and they returned to their own homes.
verses.21:7: And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we arrived at Ptolemais; and having greeted the brethren, we stayed with them one day.
verses.21:8: On the next day we departed and came to Caesarea, and entering the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we stayed with him.
verses.21:9: Now this man had four virgin daughters who prophesied.
verses.21:10: And as we stayed there for many days, a certain prophet named Agabus came down from Judea.
verses.21:11: When he came to us, he took Paul's belt, bound his own feet and hands, and said, "Thus says the Holy Spirit: 'In this manner the Jews in Jerusalem shall bind the man to whom this belt belongs, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.'"
verses.21:12: Now when we heard these things, both we and those of that place pleaded with him not to go up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:13: Then Paul answered, "What are you doing, weeping and breaking my heart? For I am ready not only to be bound, but also to die in Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus."
verses.21:14: And since he would not be persuaded, we fell silent, saying, "Let the will of the Lord be done."
verses.21:15: After these days we packed our baggage and went up to Jerusalem.
verses.21:16: Some of the disciples from Caesarea also went with us, bringing us to one Mnason of Cyprus, an early disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
verses.21:17: And when we arrived in Jerusalem, the brethren received us gladly.
verses.21:18: On the following day Paul went in with us to James, and all the elders were present.
verses.21:19: After greeting them, he related one by one the things which God had done among the Gentiles through his ministry.
verses.21:20: And when they heard it, they glorified God. And they said to him, "You see, brother, how many tens of thousands there are among the Jews who have believed, and they are all zealous for the law;
verses.21:21: but they have been informed about you that you teach all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to forsake Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children nor to walk according to the customs.
verses.21:22: What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come.
verses.21:23: Therefore do this that we tell you: we have four men who have taken a vow upon themselves.
verses.21:24: Take them and be purified with them, and pay their expenses so that they may shave their heads, and all will know that there is nothing in the things of which they have been informed concerning you, but that you yourself also walk in an orderly manner, keeping the law.
verses.21:25: But concerning the Gentiles who have believed, we have written, having decided that they should keep themselves from what is offered to idols, from blood, from what is strangled, and from sexual immorality."
verses.21:26: Then Paul took the men, and on the next day, having been purified with them, he entered the temple, announcing the completion of the days of purification, until the offering was presented for each one of them.
verses.21:27: Now when the seven days were nearly completed, the Jews from Asia, seeing him in the temple, stirred up the whole crowd and laid hands on him,
verses.21:28: crying out, "Men of Israel, help! This is the man who teaches everyone everywhere against the people, the law, and this place; and furthermore he has even brought Greeks into the temple and has defiled this holy place."
verses.21:29: For they had previously seen Trophimus the Ephesian with him in the city, and they supposed that Paul had brought him into the temple.
verses.21:30: And the whole city was stirred up, and the people ran together; and seizing Paul, they dragged him out of the temple, and immediately the doors were shut.
verses.21:31: Now as they were seeking to kill him, a report went up to the commander of the cohort that all Jerusalem was in an uproar.
verses.21:32: At once he took soldiers and centurions and ran down to them; and when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they stopped beating Paul.
verses.21:33: Then the commander came near and took hold of him, and commanded him to be bound with two chains; and he inquired who he was and what he had done.
verses.21:34: And some in the crowd were shouting one thing and some another; so when he could not ascertain the truth because of the tumult, he commanded him to be brought into the barracks.
verses.21:35: When he reached the stairs, he had to be carried by the soldiers because of the violence of the crowd;
verses.21:36: for the multitude of the people kept following, crying out, "Away with him!"
verses.21:37: As Paul was about to be led into the barracks, he said to the commander, "May I say something to you?" And he replied, "Do you know Greek?
verses.21:38: Are you not, then, the Egyptian who before these days stirred up a revolt and led the four thousand men of the Assassins out into the wilderness?"
verses.21:39: But Paul said, "I am a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia, a citizen of no insignificant city; and I implore you, permit me to speak to the people."
verses.21:40: And when he had given him permission, Paul stood on the stairs and motioned with his hand to the people; and when there was a great silence, he addressed them in the Hebrew language, saying,
verses.22:1: "Men, brethren, and fathers, hear my defense which I now make to you."
verses.22:2: And when they heard that he was addressing them in the Hebrew language, they kept even greater silence. And he said:
verses.22:3: "I am indeed a Jew, born in Tarsus of Cilicia, yet brought up in this city at the feet of Gamaliel, educated according to the strictness of the law of our fathers, being zealous for God just as all of you are today.
verses.22:4: I persecuted this Way to the death, binding and delivering into prisons both men and women,
verses.22:5: as also the high priest bears me witness, and all the council of elders, from whom I also received letters to the brethren, and journeyed to Damascus to bring in chains even those who were there to Jerusalem to be punished.
verses.22:6: Now it came to pass, as I journeyed and drew near to Damascus about noon, that suddenly a great light from heaven shone all around me.
verses.22:7: And I fell to the ground and heard a voice saying to me, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me?'
verses.22:8: So I answered, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said to me, 'I am Jesus of Nazareth, whom you are persecuting.'
verses.22:9: And those who were with me indeed saw the light, but they did not hear the voice of Him who spoke to me.
verses.22:10: Then I said, 'What shall I do, Lord?' And the Lord said to me, 'Arise and go into Damascus, and there you will be told of all things which are appointed for you to do.'
verses.22:11: And since I could not see because of the glory of that light, I was led by the hand by those who were with me, and came into Damascus.
verses.22:12: Then a certain Ananias, a devout man according to the law, well spoken of by all the Jews who dwelt there,
verses.22:13: came to me; and standing beside me, he said to me, 'Brother Saul, receive your sight.' And at that very hour I looked up at him.
verses.22:14: Then he said, 'The God of our fathers has appointed you to know His will, and to see the Righteous One, and to hear a voice from His mouth.
verses.22:15: For you shall be a witness for Him to all men of what you have seen and heard.
verses.22:16: And now why do you delay? Arise, be baptized, and wash away your sins, calling on His name.'
verses.22:17: Now it came to pass, when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance
verses.22:18: and saw Him saying to me, 'Make haste and depart quickly out of Jerusalem, because they will not receive your testimony concerning Me.'
verses.22:19: And I said, 'Lord, they themselves know that in every synagogue I imprisoned and beat those who believe in You;
verses.22:20: and when the blood of Your witness Stephen was being shed, I myself also was standing by and approving, and guarding the garments of those who were slaying him.'
verses.22:21: And He said to me, 'Go, for I will send you far away to the Gentiles.'"
verses.22:22: And they listened to him up to this word, and then they lifted up their voices and said, "Away with such a man from the earth, for he ought not to live!"
verses.22:23: And as they were shouting, throwing off their garments, and flinging dust into the air,
verses.22:24: the commander ordered him to be brought into the barracks, saying that he should be examined by scourging, so that he might find out for what reason they were shouting thus against him.
verses.22:25: But when they had stretched him out with the leather straps, Paul said to the centurion who stood by, "Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and uncondemned?"
verses.22:26: When the centurion heard this, he went to the commander and reported it, saying, "What are you about to do? For this man is a Roman."
verses.22:27: Then the commander came and said to him, "Tell me, are you a Roman?" And he said, "Yes."
verses.22:28: The commander answered, "With a large sum I acquired this citizenship." And Paul said, "But I was even born a citizen."
verses.22:29: Immediately, therefore, those who were about to examine him withdrew from him; and the commander himself was also afraid when he learned that he was a Roman, and because he had bound him.
verses.22:30: On the next day, wishing to know with certainty why he was accused by the Jews, he unbound him and commanded the chief priests and all the council to assemble, and brought Paul down and set him before them.
verses.23:1: Then Paul, gazing intently at the council, said, "Men and brethren, I have conducted my life in all good conscience before God until this day."
verses.23:2: And the high priest Ananias commanded those standing beside him to strike his mouth.
verses.23:3: Then Paul said to him, "God is about to strike you, you whitewashed wall! And do you sit judging me according to the law, yet contrary to the law command me to be struck?"
verses.23:4: And those who stood by said, "Do you revile the high priest of God?"
verses.23:5: Then Paul said, "I did not know, brethren, that he is the high priest; for it is written, 'You shall not speak evil of a ruler of your people.'"
verses.23:6: Now when Paul perceived that the one part were Sadducees and the other Pharisees, he cried out in the council, "Men and brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of Pharisees; concerning the hope and resurrection of the dead I am being judged!"
verses.23:7: And as he spoke this, a dissension arose between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
verses.23:8: For Sadducees say that there is no resurrection—neither angel nor spirit—but Pharisees confess both.
verses.23:9: Then there arose a great outcry, and certain of the scribes of the Pharisees' party stood up and contended sharply, saying, "We find nothing evil in this man; and if a spirit has spoken to him, or an angel—"
verses.23:10: And when a great dissension arose, the commander, fearing lest Paul be torn in pieces by them, ordered the soldiers to go down and seize him from their midst, and to bring him into the barracks.
verses.23:11: Now on the following night the Lord stood by him and said, "Be of good courage; for as you have solemnly testified concerning Me in Jerusalem, so you must also bear witness in Rome."
verses.23:12: And when day came, the Jews formed a conspiracy and bound themselves under a curse, saying that they would neither eat nor drink until they had slain Paul.
verses.23:13: Now there were more than forty who had made this plot.
verses.23:14: They came to the chief priests and the elders and said, "We have bound ourselves under a solemn curse to taste nothing until we have slain Paul.
verses.23:15: Now therefore, you, together with the council, give notice to the commander that he should bring him down to you, as though you were about to examine the matters concerning him more accurately; and we, before he draws near, are ready to put him to death."
verses.23:16: But when the son of Paul's sister heard of the ambush, he came and entered the barracks and reported it to Paul.
verses.23:17: Then Paul called one of the centurions to him and said, "Lead this young man to the commander, for he has something to report to him."
verses.23:18: So he took him and brought him to the commander and said, "Paul the prisoner called me to him and asked me to bring this young man to you, since he has something to tell you."
verses.23:19: Then the commander took him by the hand, withdrew privately, and inquired, "What is it that you have to report to me?"
verses.23:20: And he said, "The Jews have agreed to ask you to bring Paul down to the council tomorrow, as though you were about to inquire somewhat more accurately concerning him.
verses.23:21: Do not be persuaded by them, therefore; for more than forty men from among them lie in ambush for him, who have bound themselves under a curse neither to eat nor to drink until they have put him to death; and now they are ready, awaiting the promise from you."
verses.23:22: So the commander dismissed the young man, charging him, "Tell no one that you have disclosed these things to me."
verses.23:23: And he called two of the centurions to him and said, "Make ready two hundred soldiers to go as far as Caesarea, along with seventy horsemen and two hundred spearmen, at the third hour of the night,"
verses.23:24: and he told them to provide mounts on which to place Paul, that they might bring him safely to Felix the governor.
verses.23:25: He also wrote a letter having this form:
verses.23:26: "Claudius Lysias, to the most excellent governor Felix: Greetings.
verses.23:27: This man was seized by the Jews and was about to be put to death by them, when I came upon them with the troops and rescued him, having learned that he is a Roman.
verses.23:28: And desiring to know the charge for which they were accusing him, I brought him down into their council.
verses.23:29: I found him to be accused concerning questions of their law, yet having no charge worthy of death or of chains.
verses.23:30: And when it was disclosed to me that there would be a plot against the man, I sent him to you at once, having also commanded his accusers to speak against him before you."
verses.23:31: So the soldiers, according to what had been commanded them, took Paul and brought him by night to Antipatris.
verses.23:32: And on the next day, leaving the horsemen to go on with him, they returned to the barracks.
verses.23:33: When these entered Caesarea and delivered the letter to the governor, they also presented Paul before him.
verses.23:34: And when he had read it and asked from what province he was, and learned that he was from Cilicia,
verses.23:35: "I will hear you fully," he said, "when your accusers also have arrived," and he commanded him to be kept under guard in Herod's Praetorium.
verses.24:1: Now after five days the high priest Ananias came down with certain elders and a certain orator named Tertullus, and they laid their case before the governor against Paul.
verses.24:2: And when he was summoned, Tertullus began to accuse him, saying, "Since through you we enjoy great peace, and reforms are being brought about for this nation through your foresight,
verses.24:3: we accept it in every way and in every place, most excellent Felix, with all thankfulness.
verses.24:4: Yet lest I detain you any further, I implore you to hear us briefly in your graciousness.
verses.24:5: For we have found this man to be a plague, one who stirs up dissensions among all the Jews throughout the inhabited world, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
verses.24:6: who even attempted to profane the temple, and whom we also seized;
verses.24:8: from whom, by examining him yourself, you will be able to ascertain concerning all these things of which we accuse him."
verses.24:9: And the Jews also joined in the charge, affirming that these things were so.
verses.24:10: Then Paul, after the governor had nodded to him to speak, answered, "Knowing that for many years you have been a judge over this nation, I gladly make my defense concerning myself,
verses.24:11: since you are able to ascertain that it has been no more than twelve days since I went up to Jerusalem to worship.
verses.24:12: And neither in the temple did they find me disputing with anyone or stirring up a crowd, nor in the synagogues, nor throughout the city;
verses.24:13: nor are they able to prove to you the things of which they now accuse me.
verses.24:14: Yet this I confess to you, that according to the Way, which they call a sect, so I worship the God of our fathers, believing all things that are according to the Law and that are written in the Prophets,
verses.24:15: having a hope in God, which these men themselves also await, that there is about to be a resurrection both of the righteous and of the unrighteous.
verses.24:16: In view of this, I myself also strive to keep a blameless conscience toward God and men at all times.
verses.24:17: Now after many years I came to bring alms to my nation, and offerings,
verses.24:18: in the midst of which they found me purified in the temple, neither with a crowd nor with tumult.
verses.24:19: But there were certain Jews from Asia, who ought to have been present before you and to bring accusation if they had anything against me;
verses.24:20: or else let these men themselves say what wrongdoing they found when I stood before the council,
verses.24:21: other than this one statement which I cried out while standing among them, 'Concerning the resurrection of the dead I am being judged before you this day.'"
verses.24:22: Then Felix, having more accurate knowledge of the matters concerning the Way, adjourned them, saying, "When Lysias the commander comes down, I will decide your case."
verses.24:23: And he gave orders to the centurion that he should be kept under guard, yet have some liberty, and that none of his own people should be hindered from ministering to him.
verses.24:24: Now after some days, when Felix arrived with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, he sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ Jesus.
verses.24:25: And as he reasoned about righteousness, self-control, and the judgment to come, Felix became terrified and answered, "Go your way for now; and when I have an opportune time, I will summon you."
verses.24:26: At the same time he was also hoping that money would be given him by Paul; therefore he sent for him the more frequently and conversed with him.
verses.24:27: Now when two years had been fulfilled, Felix received Porcius Festus as his successor; and desiring to do the Jews a favor, Felix left Paul in chains.
verses.25:1: Now when Festus had entered upon his province, after three days he went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem.
verses.25:2: And the chief priests and the foremost men of the Jews brought formal charges before him against Paul, and they urged him,
verses.25:3: asking a favor against him, that he would send for him to Jerusalem, while preparing an ambush to slay him along the way.
verses.25:4: Festus, however, answered that Paul was being kept in custody at Caesarea, and that he himself was about to depart shortly.
verses.25:5: "Therefore," he said, "let those among you who hold authority go down with me, and if there is anything amiss in this man, let them accuse him."
verses.25:6: And having stayed among them not more than eight or ten days, he went down to Caesarea; and on the next day, sitting upon the judgment seat, he commanded Paul to be brought in.
verses.25:7: When he had arrived, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood round about him, bringing many and grievous charges which they were unable to prove,
verses.25:8: while Paul spoke in his own defense: "Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar have I sinned in anything."
verses.25:9: But Festus, wishing to gain favor with the Jews, answered Paul and said, "Are you willing to go up to Jerusalem and there be judged before me concerning these matters?"
verses.25:10: Then Paul said, "I stand before the judgment seat of Caesar, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as you also know very well.
verses.25:11: If indeed I am an offender and have committed anything worthy of death, I do not refuse to die; yet if there is nothing in these charges which they bring against me, no one can hand me over to them as a favor. I appeal to Caesar."
verses.25:12: Then Festus, having conferred with the council, answered, "To Caesar you have appealed; to Caesar you shall go."
verses.25:13: Now when some days had passed, King Agrippa and Bernice arrived at Caesarea to greet Festus.
verses.25:14: And as they lingered there many days, Festus laid Paul's case before the king, saying, "There is a certain man left behind as a prisoner by Felix,
verses.25:15: concerning whom, when I was in Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews brought formal charges, asking for a sentence of condemnation against him.
verses.25:16: To them I answered that it is not the custom of the Romans to surrender any man as a favor before the accused faces his accusers and receives opportunity to make his defense concerning the charge.
verses.25:17: Therefore, when they had assembled here, making no delay, on the following day I sat upon the judgment seat and commanded the man to be brought in.
verses.25:18: When the accusers stood up concerning him, they brought no charge of such evil deeds as I had supposed,
verses.25:19: but they had certain points of dispute with him concerning their own religion, and concerning a certain Jesus, who was dead, whom Paul asserted to be alive.
verses.25:20: And because I was at a loss how to inquire into these matters, I asked whether he was willing to go to Jerusalem and there be judged concerning them.
verses.25:21: But when Paul appealed to be kept in custody for the decision of Augustus, I commanded him to be kept until I might send him up to Caesar."
verses.25:22: Then Agrippa said to Festus, "I myself would also like to hear the man." "Tomorrow," he said, "you shall hear him."
verses.25:23: So on the next day, when Agrippa and Bernice had come with great pomp and had entered the audience hall together with the commanders and the prominent men of the city, at Festus's command Paul was brought in.
verses.25:24: And Festus said, "King Agrippa, and all you men who are present here with us, you behold this man concerning whom the whole multitude of the Jews petitioned me, both in Jerusalem and here, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
verses.25:25: Yet I found that he had committed nothing worthy of death, and since he himself appealed to Augustus, I determined to send him.
verses.25:26: Concerning him I have nothing definite to write to my lord. Therefore I have brought him forth before you, and especially before you, King Agrippa, so that after the examination has taken place I may have something to write.
verses.25:27: For it seems unreasonable to me, when sending a prisoner, not also to indicate the charges against him."
verses.26:1: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "You are permitted to speak for yourself." So Paul stretched forth his hand and made his defense:
verses.26:2: "Concerning all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, King Agrippa, I count myself fortunate that I am to make my defense before you today,
verses.26:3: especially because you are well acquainted with all the customs and controversies among the Jews; therefore I implore you to hear me patiently.
verses.26:4: My manner of life from my youth, which from the beginning was spent among my own nation and in Jerusalem, all the Jews know,
verses.26:5: having known me from the first, if they are willing to testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived as a Pharisee.
verses.26:6: And now I stand on trial for the hope of the promise made by God to our fathers,
verses.26:7: to which our twelve tribes, earnestly worshiping night and day, hope to attain. Concerning this hope, O king, I am accused by the Jews.
verses.26:8: Why is it judged incredible among you if God raises the dead?
verses.26:9: Indeed, I myself once thought that I ought to do many things in opposition to the name of Jesus of Nazareth.
verses.26:10: This I also did in Jerusalem; and many of the saints I locked up in prisons, having received authority from the chief priests, and when they were being put to death, I cast my vote against them.
verses.26:11: And punishing them often in every synagogue, I sought to compel them to blaspheme; and being exceedingly enraged against them, I persecuted them even as far as foreign cities.
verses.26:12: While engaged in these things, as I was journeying to Damascus with authority and a commission from the chief priests,
verses.26:13: at midday along the road, O king, I saw a light from heaven, surpassing the splendor of the sun, shining round about me and those who were journeying with me.
verses.26:14: And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me in the Hebrew tongue, 'Saul, Saul, why are you persecuting Me? It is hard for you to kick against the goads.'
verses.26:15: And I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And the Lord said, 'I am Jesus, whom you are persecuting.
verses.26:16: But rise and stand upon your feet; for to this purpose I have appeared to you, to appoint you as a servant and a witness both of the things in which you have seen Me and of those in which I will yet appear to you,
verses.26:17: delivering you from the people and from the Gentiles, to whom I am sending you,
verses.26:18: to open their eyes, so that they may turn from darkness to light and from the dominion of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins and an inheritance among those who have been sanctified by faith in Me.'
verses.26:19: Therefore, King Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
verses.26:20: but declared first to those in Damascus and in Jerusalem, and throughout all the region of Judea, and also to the Gentiles, that they should repent and turn to God, performing deeds worthy of repentance.
verses.26:21: On account of these things the Jews seized me in the temple and attempted to slay me.
verses.26:22: Having therefore obtained help from God, I stand to this day bearing witness to both small and great, saying nothing beyond what both the prophets and Moses spoke as things that would come to pass:
verses.26:23: that the Christ must suffer, and that, being the first from the resurrection of the dead, He would proclaim light both to the people and to the Gentiles."
verses.26:24: Now as he was speaking these things in his defense, Festus cried out with a loud voice, "You are mad, Paul! Your great learning is turning you to madness!"
verses.26:25: But Paul said, "I am not mad, most excellent Festus, but I utter words of truth and soberness.
verses.26:26: For the king knows concerning these matters, to whom I also speak with boldness; for I am convinced that none of these things has escaped his notice, since this has not been done in a corner.
verses.26:27: King Agrippa, do you believe the prophets? I know that you believe."
verses.26:28: Then Agrippa said to Paul, "In so short a time would you persuade and make me a Christian?"
verses.26:29: And Paul said, "I would pray to God that, whether in a short time or a long, not only you, but also all who hear me today, might become such as I also am—except for these chains."
verses.26:30: Then the king arose, and the governor, and Bernice, and those who sat with them;
verses.26:31: and when they had withdrawn, they spoke with one another, saying, "This man is doing nothing worthy of death or of chains."
verses.26:32: And Agrippa said to Festus, "This man might have been set at liberty if he had not appealed to Caesar."
verses.27:1: Now when it was decided that we should sail away to Italy, they delivered both Paul and certain other prisoners to a centurion named Julius, of the Augustan Cohort.
verses.27:2: And boarding a ship of Adramyttium that was about to sail to the places along the coast of Asia, we put out to sea, Aristarchus, a Macedonian of Thessalonica, being with us.
verses.27:3: And on the next day we put in at Sidon; and Julius, treating Paul kindly, permitted him to go to his friends and receive care.
verses.27:4: And putting out to sea from there, we sailed under the shelter of Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
verses.27:5: And having sailed across the open sea off Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came down to Myra in Lycia.
verses.27:6: And there the centurion found an Alexandrian ship sailing to Italy, and put us aboard it.
verses.27:7: Now sailing slowly for many days, and arriving with difficulty off Cnidus, since the wind did not permit us to proceed further, we sailed under the shelter of Crete off Salmone.
verses.27:8: And coasting along it with difficulty, we came to a certain place called Fair Havens, near which was the city of Lasea.
verses.27:9: Now when much time had elapsed, and the voyage was now hazardous because the Fast had already gone by, Paul admonished them,
verses.27:10: saying to them, "Men, I perceive that the voyage will be with injury and great loss, not only of the cargo and of the ship, but also of our lives."
verses.27:11: Yet the centurion was persuaded more by the helmsman and the shipowner than by the things spoken by Paul.
verses.27:12: And since the harbor was unsuitable to winter in, the majority gave counsel to put out to sea from there, if by any means they might reach Phoenix and winter there, a harbor of Crete facing toward the southwest and toward the northwest.
verses.27:13: Now when a gentle south wind blew, supposing that they had attained their purpose, they weighed anchor and coasted close along Crete.
verses.27:14: But not long afterward, a tempestuous wind called Euraquilo struck down from the island.
verses.27:15: And when the ship was caught and could not face into the wind, we gave way and were driven along.
verses.27:16: And running under the shelter of a small island called Clauda, we were scarcely able to gain control of the ship's boat.
verses.27:17: When they had hoisted it aboard, they used supports to undergird the ship; and fearing lest they should run aground on the Syrtis, they lowered the gear, and thus were driven along.
verses.27:18: And because we were violently storm-tossed, on the next day they began casting the cargo overboard,
verses.27:19: and on the third day with their own hands they cast out the tackle of the ship.
verses.27:20: Now when neither sun nor stars appeared for many days, and no small tempest pressed upon us, all hope that we would be saved was at last taken away.
verses.27:21: And after long abstinence from food, Paul stood in the midst of them and said, "Men, you ought indeed to have heeded me and not to have put out to sea from Crete, and thus to have avoided this injury and loss.
verses.27:22: And now I urge you to take heart, for there shall be no loss of life among you, but only of the ship.
verses.27:23: For there stood by me this night an angel of the God whose I am and whom I also serve,
verses.27:24: saying, 'Do not be afraid, Paul; you must stand before Caesar; and behold, God has graciously granted to you all those who sail with you.'
verses.27:25: Therefore take heart, men, for I believe God that it shall be just as it has been spoken to me.
verses.27:26: However, we must run aground on a certain island."
verses.27:27: Now when the fourteenth night had come, as we were driven to and fro in the Adriatic Sea, about midnight the sailors surmised that some land was drawing near to them.
verses.27:28: And taking soundings, they found twenty fathoms; and when they had gone a little farther and taken soundings again, they found fifteen fathoms.
verses.27:29: And fearing lest somewhere we should run aground on rocky places, they cast four anchors from the stern and prayed for day to come.
verses.27:30: Now as the sailors were seeking to flee from the ship, and had lowered the ship's boat into the sea under pretense of intending to lay out anchors from the bow,
verses.27:31: Paul said to the centurion and to the soldiers, "Unless these men remain in the ship, you cannot be saved."
verses.27:32: Then the soldiers cut away the ropes of the ship's boat and let it fall away.
verses.27:33: And as day was about to dawn, Paul urged them all to partake of food, saying, "Today is the fourteenth day you have continued in suspense without food, having taken nothing.
verses.27:34: Therefore I urge you to partake of food, for this is for your survival; for not a hair from the head of any one of you shall perish."
verses.27:35: And when he had spoken these things and taken bread, he gave thanks to God in the presence of all, and having broken it, he began to eat.
verses.27:36: Then they all took heart, and they also partook of food.
verses.27:37: Now we were in all two hundred and seventy-six souls in the ship.
verses.27:38: And when they had been satisfied with food, they lightened the ship by casting the wheat out into the sea.
verses.27:39: Now when day came, they did not recognize the land; yet they observed a certain bay having a beach, onto which they planned, if they were able, to drive the ship.
verses.27:40: And casting off the anchors, they left them in the sea, at the same time loosening the ropes of the rudders; and hoisting the foresail to the blowing wind, they made for the beach.
verses.27:41: But striking a place where two seas met, they ran the vessel aground; and the bow stuck fast and remained immovable, while the stern was being broken up by the violence.
verses.27:42: And the soldiers' plan was to kill the prisoners, lest any of them should swim away and escape.
verses.27:43: But the centurion, wishing to save Paul, restrained them from their purpose, and commanded those who were able to swim to cast themselves overboard first and get to land,
verses.27:44: and the rest, some on planks and others on pieces from the ship. And so it came to pass that all were brought safely to land.
verses.28:1: Now when we had been brought safely ashore, we then learned that the island was called Malta.
verses.28:2: And the native people showed us no ordinary kindness, for they kindled a fire and welcomed us all because of the rain that had set in and because of the cold.
verses.28:3: But when Paul had gathered a bundle of sticks and laid them upon the fire, a viper came out because of the heat and fastened onto his hand.
verses.28:4: So when the native people saw the creature hanging from his hand, they said to one another, "Without doubt this man is a murderer, whom, though he was delivered from the sea, Justice has not permitted to live."
verses.28:5: He, however, shook off the creature into the fire and suffered no harm.
verses.28:6: Yet they were expecting that he would swell up or suddenly fall down dead. But after they had waited a long time and saw nothing amiss happening to him, they changed their minds and began saying that he was a god.
verses.28:7: Now in the region around that place were estates belonging to the leading man of the island, named Publius, who welcomed us and hospitably lodged us for three days.
verses.28:8: And it came to pass that the father of Publius lay ill, afflicted with fevers and dysentery. Paul went in to him, and having prayed, laid his hands on him and healed him.
verses.28:9: When this had taken place, the rest of those on the island who had infirmities also came and were healed.
verses.28:10: They also honored us with many honors, and when we set sail, they put on board whatever things were needed.
verses.28:11: After three months we set sail in an Alexandrian ship that had wintered at the island, bearing the figurehead of the Twin Brothers.
verses.28:12: And putting in at Syracuse, we stayed there three days.
verses.28:13: From there we weighed anchor and arrived at Rhegium. And after one day a south wind sprang up, and on the second day we came to Puteoli,
verses.28:14: where we found brethren and were invited to remain with them seven days. And so we came to Rome.
verses.28:15: And from there the brethren, having heard of us, came out to meet us as far as the Forum of Appius and Three Taverns. When Paul saw them, he gave thanks to God and took courage.
verses.28:16: Now when we entered Rome, Paul was permitted to dwell by himself with the soldier who guarded him.
verses.28:17: And it came to pass after three days that he called together the chief men of the Jews. When they had assembled, he said to them, "Men and brethren, though I had done nothing contrary to the people or the customs of our fathers, yet I was delivered as a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans,
verses.28:18: who, when they had examined me, wished to release me, because there was no ground for death in me.
verses.28:19: But when the Jews spoke against it, I was compelled to appeal to Caesar—not that I had anything of which to accuse my nation.
verses.28:20: For this reason therefore I have asked to see you and to speak with you, because for the sake of the hope of Israel I am bound with this chain."
verses.28:21: Then they said to him, "We have neither received letters from Judea concerning you, nor has any of the brethren who came reported or spoken anything evil about you.
verses.28:22: Yet we desire to hear from you what your views are; for concerning this sect, it is known to us that it is spoken against everywhere."
verses.28:23: So when they had appointed him a day, they came to him at his lodging in greater numbers, to whom he expounded, solemnly testifying of the kingdom of God and seeking to persuade them concerning Jesus from both the Law of Moses and the Prophets, from morning until evening.
verses.28:24: And some were persuaded by the things that were spoken, and others disbelieved.
verses.28:25: So, being in disagreement among themselves, they began to depart after Paul had spoken one statement: "The Holy Spirit spoke rightly through Isaiah the prophet to your fathers,
verses.28:26: saying, 'Go to this people and say: Hearing you will hear and shall by no means understand, and seeing you will see and shall by no means perceive;
verses.28:27: for the heart of this people has grown dull, and with their ears they have scarcely heard, and they have closed their eyes, lest they should see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart and turn, and I should heal them.'
verses.28:28: Therefore let it be known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the Gentiles, and they will indeed listen."
verses.28:30: Now he remained two full years in his own rented dwelling, and welcomed all who came to him,
verses.28:31: proclaiming the kingdom of God and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all boldness, without hindrance.

notes.1:4: The Greek participle synalizomenos means either "gathered together with them" or "eating together with them" (literally sharing salt at a meal).
notes.1:12: A Sabbath day's journey was the traditional maximum distance permitted for travel on the Sabbath, approximately two thousand cubits (roughly half to three-quarters of a mile).
notes.1:18: The Greek phrase prenes genomenos is traditionally rendered "falling headlong" (face downward), though some interpreters take it in a medical sense meaning "swelling up."
notes.1:25: The Greek critical text reads topon ("place"), creating a deliberate wordplay with Judas departing to "his own place," whereas later manuscripts read kleron ("lot" or "share").
notes.2:24: The phrase "pangs of death" reflects the Septuagint rendering of Psalm 18:4-5 (where the Hebrew word for cords or snares is translated as birth pangs), creating the vivid image of God loosing the agonies of death.
notes.2:30: The critical Greek text reads simply "to seat one from the fruit of his loins upon his throne," omitting the later Byzantine expansion "according to the flesh, He would raise up the Christ."
notes.2:33: The Greek dative phrase may be understood either directionally ("to the right hand of God," echoing Psalm 110:1) or instrumentally ("by the right hand of God").
notes.2:47: The critical Greek text ends with "epi to auto" (literally "together," rendered here as "to their number"), whereas later manuscripts read "to the church."
notes.3:6: The Greek critical text reads simply "walk" without the longer Byzantine addition "rise up and walk."
notes.3:13: Greek pais means "Servant" (echoing the Septuagint Servant Songs of Isaiah) rather than merely "child," a messianic title recurring in 3:26, 4:27, and 4:30.
notes.3:15: Greek archegos carries the sense of "Author," "Originator," or "Prince," denoting the one who pioneers and imparts life.
notes.3:22: The Greek critical text reads "the Lord our God," whereas many manuscripts harmonize with Deuteronomy 18:15 to read "your God."
notes.4:9: Greek sesostai ("has been made whole" or "healed") is from the same verb (sozo) translated "be saved" in 4:12, linking the man's physical restoration to spiritual salvation.
notes.4:25: The Greek text contains a compressed, grammatically difficult phrase combining "our father," "through the Holy Spirit," and "by the mouth of David Your servant," rendered here according to its evident sense.
notes.4:26: Greek tou christou autou literally means "His Anointed" or "His Christ," echoing Psalm 2:2 (LXX) and linking directly to "whom You anointed" in 4:27.
notes.4:36: The Greek critical text reads "Joseph" rather than the later Byzantine variant "Joses."
notes.5:28: The critical Greek text reads a direct statement here rather than a question ("Did we not strictly charge you...?" in later manuscripts), underscoring the high priest's blunt accusation.
notes.5:31: The Greek dative phrase can be rendered either locatively ("to His right hand") or instrumentally ("by His right hand"), and "Prince" (Greek archegos) carries the sense of leader, pioneer, or author.
notes.5:39: The critical Greek text reads the future "you will not be able to overthrow them" (referring to the apostles), whereas later manuscripts read "you cannot overthrow it" (referring to the work).
notes.5:41: The critical Greek text reads simply "the Name" without a possessive pronoun, using it as an absolute reverential designation for Jesus.
notes.6:1: "Hellenists" refers to Greek-speaking Jews, while "Hebrews" refers to Jews whose primary language was Aramaic or Hebrew.
notes.6:3: The critical Greek text reads "full of the Spirit" without an adjective, whereas later manuscripts add "Holy."
notes.6:8: The critical Greek text reads "full of grace and power," whereas later manuscripts read "full of faith and power."
notes.6:9: "Freedmen" (Greek Libertinoi, from Latin libertini) designates formerly enslaved Jews or their descendants who had been emancipated, likely having settled in Jerusalem from Rome.
notes.7:14: "Seventy-five souls" follows the Septuagint reading of Genesis 46:27 and Exodus 1:5, whereas the Hebrew Masoretic Text numbers Jacob's household at seventy.
notes.7:16: The critical Greek text reads "in Shechem" (rather than "the father of Shechem" in later manuscripts). Stephen compresses into one summary Abraham's purchase of the burial cave at Machpelah (Genesis 23) and Jacob's purchase of land from the sons of Hamor at Shechem (Genesis 33:19; Joshua 24:32).
notes.7:20: The Greek phrase "fair in the sight of God" (asteios to theo) may also function as a Semitic superlative meaning "exceedingly fair" or "extraordinarily beautiful."
notes.7:30: The critical Greek text reads simply "an angel" (angelos), whereas later Byzantine manuscripts add "of the Lord."
notes.7:38: The critical Greek text reads "to give to you" (hymin), underscoring Stephen's direct address to his hearers, whereas other manuscripts read "to give to us" (hemin).
notes.7:43: "Rompha" transliterates the critical Greek reading Rompha (cf. Septuagint Amos 5:26 Raiphan, later manuscripts Remphan, and Hebrew Kiyyun), the name of a pagan star-god associated with Saturn.
notes.7:46: The critical Greek text reads "for the house of Jacob" (to oiko Iakob), whereas later manuscripts harmonize with Psalm 132:5 by reading "for the God of Jacob" (to theo Iakob).
notes.8:5: The Greek text reads "the city of Samaria" with the definite article, likely referring to the capital city of the region, whereas some manuscripts omit the article ("a city of Samaria").
notes.8:26: The Greek phrase rendered "toward the south" can also mean "at noon." The final remark may refer either to the desert route itself or to the uninhabited site of Old Gaza.
notes.8:33: Verses 32 and 33 follow the Septuagint text of Isaiah 53:7-8 rather than the Masoretic Hebrew wording; the critical Greek text also reads "In humiliation" without "His."
notes.8:36: The earliest Greek manuscripts move directly from verse 36 to verse 38 without the later confession of faith traditionally numbered as verse 37.
notes.9:5: The critical Greek text omits the longer expansion found in the Textus Receptus ("It is hard for you to kick against the goads..." and Saul's reply in verse 6), which entered later manuscripts from the parallel accounts in Acts 26:14 and 22:10.
notes.9:20: The critical Greek text reads "Jesus" here rather than "the Christ," which appears in later Byzantine manuscripts.
notes.9:25: The critical Greek text reads "his disciples," whereas some later manuscripts smooth the phrase to "the disciples."
notes.9:31: The critical Greek text uses the singular "the church" with singular verbs across Judea, Galilee, and Samaria, whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read the plural "the churches."
notes.10:19: The critical Greek text reads simply "men are seeking you," omitting the numeral "three" (or "two") that appears in later manuscripts to harmonize with verses 7–8.
notes.10:30: The critical Greek text omits "fasting" (present in later Byzantine manuscripts), and the Greek idiom literally meaning "from the fourth day until this hour" refers to the corresponding hour of the day four days earlier.
notes.10:36: Verses 36–38 display loose, emphatic Greek syntax (anacoluthon), moving from the opening accusative "the word which He sent" (v. 36) to "the event that came to pass" (v. 37) and "Jesus of Nazareth" (v. 38) as Peter summarizes the gospel message.
notes.10:48: The critical Greek text reads "in the name of Jesus Christ," whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "in the name of the Lord."
notes.11:12: The Greek active participle translated "making no distinction" (mēden diakrinanta) emphasizes making no distinction between Jew and Gentile, though it can also carry the sense "without hesitating."
notes.11:20: The Greek text reads Hellēnistas ("Hellenists," Greek-speaking people), whereas a major textual variant reads Hellēnas ("Greeks," i.e., Gentiles).
notes.11:28: Claudius reigned as Roman emperor from AD 41 to 54, during which period historical sources record severe famines, including one affecting Judea around AD 46–48.
notes.12:4: The Greek tetradion refers to a squad of four soldiers (sixteen in total), rotating watches with two chained beside Peter and two guarding the prison door (cf. v. 6).
notes.12:19: Literally "led away" (apachthēnai), a standard Greek legal euphemism for being led off to execution.
notes.12:25: The Greek text reads eis Ierousalēm ("to Jerusalem"), punctuated here with "having fulfilled their ministry," while other manuscripts read ex or apo Ierousalēm ("returned from Jerusalem").
notes.13:18: The Greek text reads etropophoresen ("bore with their ways"), whereas some manuscripts differ by one letter and read etrophophoresen ("cared for" or "nursed," echoing Deuteronomy 1:31 LXX).
notes.13:20: In the Greek critical text, "about four hundred and fifty years" concludes the preceding period (the sojourn in Egypt, the wilderness wandering, and the inheritance of Canaan) rather than modifying the era of the judges.
notes.13:26: The Greek critical text reads "to us" (hemin), including Paul and his Jewish hearers together, whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "to you" (hymin).
notes.13:33: The Greek critical text reads "for our children" (tois teknois hemon), whereas later manuscripts read "for us, their children."
notes.14:12: The Greek text names Zeus and Hermes directly, whereas older English versions followed the Latin Vulgate in substituting their Roman equivalents, Jupiter and Mercury.
notes.14:17: The Greek critical text reads the second-person plural "you" and "your," rather than "us" and "our" found in some later manuscripts.
notes.14:23: The Greek verb cheirotoneo originally meant to elect by raising the hand and came in Koine Greek to denote formally appointing leaders.
notes.15:14: "Simeon" reflects the Semitic form Symeon used here by James to refer to Simon Peter.
notes.15:17: James cites Amos 9:11-12 according to the Greek Septuagint ("that the remnant of mankind may seek the Lord"), which differs from the Hebrew Masoretic Text ("that they may possess the remnant of Edom").
notes.15:18: The critical Greek text ends concisely with "known from of old" completing the clause from verse 17, whereas later Byzantine manuscripts expand it into "Known to God from eternity are all His works."
notes.15:23: The critical text reads "the apostles and the elders, brethren" in apposition, omitting the conjunction "and" found in later manuscripts.
notes.15:33: Verse 34 ("However, it seemed good to Silas to remain there") is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts and is omitted in the Saints Greek Critical Text.
notes.16:7: The Greek text reads "the Spirit of Jesus" (a rare New Testament title emphasizing the Spirit as sent by the risen Christ); some later manuscripts read simply "the Spirit."
notes.16:12: The Greek phrase rendered "a foremost city of that district of Macedonia" is grammatically debated; it may denote either Philippi's prominence within its Macedonian subdivision or a city of the first district of Macedonia.
notes.16:16: Literally "a Python spirit," referring to the mantic spirit associated in Greek antiquity with the Delphic oracle of Apollo.
notes.16:31: The Greek text reads simply "the Lord Jesus," without "Christ" as found in some later manuscripts.
notes.17:6: "City magistrates" translates Greek politarchas ("politarchs"), the specific local title attested in inscriptions for the civic rulers of Thessalonica.
notes.17:18: "Babbler" renders Greek spermologos (literally "seed-picker"), a disparaging Athenian slang term for an intellectual scavenger who collects and repeats scraps of borrowed ideas.
notes.17:23: The critical Greek text uses neuter pronouns ("what... this") rather than the masculine pronouns ("whom... Him") found in later manuscripts.
notes.17:26: The critical Greek text reads simply ex henos ("from one [man]"), without the word haimatos ("blood") that appears in later manuscripts.
notes.18:5: The critical Greek text reads "occupied with the word" (to logo) rather than "constrained in the spirit" (to pneumati), which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.18:17: The critical Greek text reads simply "all" (pantes), omitting "the Greeks" (hoi Hellenes) found in later manuscripts, leaving open whether the crowd of bystanders or the thwarted accusers beat Sosthenes.
notes.18:18: The singular participle "having had his hair cut short" most naturally refers to Paul as the subject of the sentence, though syntactically some connect it with the immediately preceding name, Aquila.
notes.18:21: The critical Greek text follows the shorter reading, omitting the clause found in later manuscripts in which Paul states that he must keep the coming feast in Jerusalem.
notes.19:16: The Greek word translated "all of them" (amphoteroi) literally means "both of them," though in Koine Greek it could also refer to all members of a group larger than two (cf. Acts 23:8).
notes.19:21: Or "in his spirit"; the Greek phrase (en to pneumati) may refer either to the leading of the Holy Spirit or to Paul's own inward resolve.
notes.19:31: "Asiarchs" (Asiarchai) were prominent civic and religious officials of the Roman province of Asia.
notes.19:33: The Greek verb synebibasan means "prompted" or "instructed"; some manuscripts read proebibasan ("pushed forward" or "drew out").
notes.19:40: Following the critical text reading with the negative particle ou ("not"); some manuscripts omit it, reading "for which we may give an account for this disorderly gathering."
notes.20:5: The critical Greek text reads proselthontes ("having arrived" or "having come"), whereas many manuscripts read proelthontes ("having gone ahead").
notes.20:22: The Greek phrase dedemenos to pneumati ("bound in the spirit") may refer either to an inward compulsion in Paul's own spirit or to being constrained by the Holy Spirit (cf. v. 23).
notes.20:28: The Greek phrase dia tou haimatos tou idiou may be rendered either "through His own blood" or "through the blood of His Own [Son]." Some Greek manuscripts also read "the church of the Lord" instead of "the church of God."
notes.20:35: This saying of the Lord Jesus is not recorded verbatim in the four Gospels, preserving an early tradition of His teaching.
notes.21:16: The Greek dative construction (attracted to the relative pronoun) is usually understood as "bringing us to one Mnason... with whom we were to lodge," though some render it "bringing with them one Mnason."
notes.21:22: The critical Greek text reads simply "What then is to be done? They will certainly hear that you have come," omitting the later Byzantine addition "the multitude must certainly assemble."
notes.21:38: "Assassins" translates Greek sikarioi (a loanword from Latin sicarii, "dagger-men"), referring to a militant faction in first-century Judea who carried concealed daggers.
notes.21:40: "The Hebrew language" (Hebraidi dialekto, here and in 22:2) is widely understood to refer to Aramaic, the Semitic vernacular spoken in Judea, though some take it as Hebrew proper.
notes.22:9: The critical text omits the Byzantine addition "and were afraid." Greek akouo ("hear") with the accusative case here can mean "hear with understanding," explaining the distinction from Acts 9:7, where his companions heard the sound (genitive).
notes.22:20: "Witness" translates Greek martyros (the source of English "martyr"). The critical text reads simply "and approving," omitting the later Byzantine addition "to his killing."
notes.22:25: The Greek phrase "stretched him out with the leather straps" refers to binding a prisoner with thongs to a post in preparation for scourging, though some render the dative as "for the whips."
notes.23:9: The Greek sentence breaks off mid-thought (aposiopesis) amid the uproar; the earliest manuscripts omit the later scribal completion "let us not fight against God."
notes.23:23: The rare Greek term dexiolaboi (literally "right-hand graspers") denotes light-armed spearmen or lancers; the third hour of the night was about nine o'clock in the evening.
notes.23:24: The Greek shifts from direct command in verse 23 to indirect discourse here (an infinitive followed by a third-person verb), reflected by closing the quotation at the end of verse 23.
notes.24:6: The earliest Greek manuscripts omit the clauses traditionally numbered as verse 7 (along with the end of verse 6 and start of verse 8 concerning Lysias), so verse 6 leads directly into verse 8 with "from whom" referring to Paul.
notes.24:18: Verses 18-19 contain a grammatical break (anacoluthon) in Greek, introducing "certain Jews from Asia" without a main verb before moving into the relative clause "who ought to have been present before you."
notes.24:24: The critical Greek text reads "Christ Jesus" rather than simply "Christ."
notes.25:6: The critical Greek text reads 'not more than eight or ten days,' whereas the later Majority Text reads 'more than ten days.'
notes.25:19: The Greek term deisidaimonia can mean either 'religion' (a polite, neutral usage suited to addressing King Agrippa) or 'superstition.'
notes.25:21: Greek Sebastos is the imperial title corresponding to Latin Augustus ('the Venerable One'), referring here to Emperor Nero.
notes.25:26: Here 'my lord' (to kyrio) is an official title referring to the Roman emperor rather than to God.
notes.26:16: The critical Greek text includes the pronoun 'Me' (literally, 'the things in which you have seen Me'), emphasizing Paul's direct encounter with the risen Christ.
notes.26:23: Greek ei ('whether') introduces declarative points of prophetic testimony, and pathetos signifies that the Messiah was appointed to suffer.
notes.26:28: Agrippa's ironic reply is famously compact: en oligo may mean 'in a short time' or 'with little effort,' and the critical text reads poiesai ('to make' or 'to act as') rather than the later variant genesthai ('to become').
notes.27:9: The Fast refers to the Day of Atonement in late September or early October, after which autumn and winter sailing on the Mediterranean became perilous.
notes.27:12: Literally looking toward the southwest wind and toward the northwest wind, a nautical expression debated as meaning either facing southwest and northwest or opening toward the northeast and southeast.
notes.27:14: Euraquilo (Greek Eurakylon) is a Greek-Latin compound denoting a violent northeasterly storm wind; later Byzantine manuscripts read Euroklydon.
notes.27:37: Some early witnesses, notably Codex Vaticanus, read about seventy-six, while the majority of manuscripts, including Sinaiticus and Alexandrinus, read two hundred and seventy-six.
notes.27:41: The earliest Greek witnesses read simply by the violence; later manuscripts add of the waves.
notes.28:11: Greek Dioskouroi ("Twin Brothers") refers to Castor and Pollux, twin deities of Greco-Roman mythology honored as protectors of seafarers.
notes.28:13: The critical Greek text reads perielontes ("casting off" or "weighing anchor"), whereas some later manuscripts read perielthontes ("making a circuit" or "tacking around").
notes.28:16: Later manuscripts add that the centurion delivered the prisoners to the captain of the guard, a clause absent from the earliest Greek witnesses followed here.
notes.28:28: Later manuscripts include a twenty-ninth verse reporting that the Jews departed with much dispute among themselves, which is absent from the earliest Greek manuscripts.
